entry.title: Verifying whether text-to-SQL queries stay correct when business rules change
entry.summary: Verifying Text-to-SQL Queries under Changing Business Semantics arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper studies how to revalidate fixed SQL queries after business definitions change, such as refund attribution, tax treatment, eligible populations and exchange-rate dates. It proposes an executable verification profile that binds the requested revision and knowledge cutoff to legal counterexample data and exact monetary comparison. In its confirmation experiment, obligation-guided checking detected 137 discrepancies versus 127 for generic ordering at the same budget.

entry.title: CIRCE: Predicting LLM Task Complexity from Constraint Structure
entry.summary: CIRCE Divines LLM Task Complexity from Constraint Structure arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces CIRCE, a method for estimating whether a problem is too complex for a large language model before the model attempts it. A cheap LLM builds a Constraint Intermediate Representation that is deterministically compiled into a constraint graph. Across seven reasoning benchmarks and four LLMs, even a randomly initialized GNN encoder improves predictions of response correctness over the strongest baseline.

entry.title: A review of random and noisy computational oracles in smooth optimization
entry.summary: Stochastic and Noisy Oracles in Smooth Continuous Optimization arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This review examines models of inexact computational oracles that supply function values, gradients, and second-order information in smooth continuous optimization. It characterizes zeroth-, first-, and second-order oracles by quantitative error bounds and introduces deterministic and stochastic oracle models, illustrated with finite-difference approximations and stochastic gradients. Using common analytical tools, it compares convergence and complexity guarantees of optimization algorithms under different oracle models.

entry.title: Payroll Fraud Detection on Synthetic HR/ERP Graphs: Comparing Rules, Path Features and GNNs
entry.summary: Payroll Fraud Detection in Synthetic HR/ERP Graphs: An Inductive Comparison of Rules, Path Features, and Graph Neural Networks arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper frames payroll-fraud screening as inductive link prediction and entity ranking on synthetic HR/ERP graphs, pairing each planted case with a matched benign twin. It compares analyst rules, explicit path features and graph neural networks across held-out organizations. A tuned gradient-boosted model on chained-join features achieved the highest overall link average precision, and the multi-hop gain was not specific to GNNs.

entry.title: Optimization methods for the Minimum Red-Blue Separating Set Problem, applied to telling human and AI text apart
entry.summary: Optimization Techniques for Solving the Minimum Red--Blue Separating Set Problem with an Application to Human--AI Text Separation arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies the Minimum Red-Blue Separating Set Problem, a problem from computational geometry, and proposes an integer programming model, preprocessing rules, a GRASP heuristic, and two exact methods. Experiments on 250 random graphs compare these approaches, finding that ILP gives the best feasible solutions, LBBD gives the strongest lower bounds, and BBC most often proves optimality. The authors also apply the method to distinguish human-written from AI-generated texts using vocabulary-based graph features.

entry.title: Grounding photo composition labels in visible evidence
entry.summary: Grounding Image Composition with Label-Conditioned Visual Evidence arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces KU-PCPE, a benchmark for photographic composition that asks models to segment the visible regions explaining why a given composition label, such as center, diagonal, or rule of thirds, applies to an image. It contains 4,093 single-annotator training masks and a 1,327-task expert test split with three masks per image-label pair. A held-out expert reaches .867 Dice against other experts, while the strongest deployable model reaches .664.

entry.title: EDU-Jev: Single-Pass Decision Models for Education
entry.summary: EDU-Jev Training System-One Decision Models for Education arXiv · Oct 30, 2026EDU-Jev is a family of single-pass decision models with 0.8B, 2B and 4B parameters, designed for education tasks that pick from a fixed set of options, such as rubric scoring or checking answers against a marking criterion. Instead of generating text, the model outputs a probability distribution over the allowed options using a pointer head. Across twelve education benchmarks, the 4B model reaches 67.6% average accuracy, 9.4 points above the strongest of five commercial decision APIs.

entry.title: BABA-Bench: A Benchmark for Testing AI Agents That Help Patients Get Care
entry.summary: BABA-Bench: Evaluating Long-Horizon Patient-Advocacy Agents arXiv · Oct 30, 2026BABA-Bench is a benchmark of 47 interactive worlds built from de-identified, real patient advocacy cases reviewed by expert advocates. Agents must find hidden information and coordinate with insurers, clinics, suppliers, pharmacies, and community organizations, while an engine checks each action for permission, evidence, and prohibitions. Across 14 frontier models and 1,974 runs, many agents reached correct outcomes through invalid routes, and providing a verified route raised pass rates substantially.

entry.title: How rounding errors in low-precision SGD affect model scaling
entry.summary: Where, When, and How Many Bits? Scaling Laws for SGD with Stochastic Rounding arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper theoretically studies how stochastic rounding (SR) affects prediction risk in low-precision training as model size, training time, and precision change. It analyzes a two-layer linear network with a fixed random first layer, trained by mini-batch SGD on Gaussian data with power-law spectra, and proves matched upper and lower bounds on prediction error for the final model and for parameter averaging. Rounding only forward features preserves the compute scaling of exact arithmetic, while rounding backward features changes it.

entry.title: bf16 Rounding Silently Discards Most RL Policy Updates: A Hidden Mismatch and a One-Line Fix
entry.summary: bf16 Rounding Silently Discards Most RL Policy Updates: A Hidden Training-Inference Mismatch and an Unbiased One-Line Fix arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper examines reinforcement learning post-training of language models, where fp32 master weights are converted to bf16 for rollouts using round-to-nearest. The authors find that most per-step updates are smaller than half a bf16 spacing and are discarded, so only 0.4-0.5% of served weights change per step on Qwen3-1.7B. They propose Fair Cast, which exports the master weights with unbiased rounding and computes the training loss on the served copy, a one-line change that outperforms round-to-nearest in most matched seed-pair comparisons.

entry.title: D2ML: Models for direct-to-biology small molecule screening, a machine learning approach for testing new compounds without purification
entry.summary: D2ML: Models for Direct-to-Biology Small Molecule Screening arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents machine learning models designed for direct-to-biology (D2B) screening data, where newly synthesized molecules are tested without purification and their concentrations are uncertain. The models predict activity from single-point screens, relative potency from crude dose-response assays, and absolute potency from purified compounds. In an experiment targeting ROS1, independently trained models guided the selection of 84 new compounds, and the most selective one reached a ROS1 IC50 of 14.7 nM with 233-fold selectivity over TRKB.

entry.title: Generating several plausible segmentation masks from one annotation per image
entry.summary: Single-Annotation, Multi-Hypothesis Segmentation with Semantic-Spatial Residual Banks arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper addresses segmentation when each training image has only one annotated mask, but the model must return a set of masks covering multiple held-out human annotations. It proposes the Semantic-Spatial Residual Bank (SSRB), which freezes a semantic bank trained with balanced assignments and learns a per-hypothesis residual from the image. Across five medical endpoints, SSRB improves held-out mask coverage at K=8 over a Probabilistic U-Net, and on BSDS it preserves the semantic bank's region grouping.

entry.title: A single MRI model that segments pancreatic tumors and nearby organs for cancer radiotherapy planning
entry.summary: Segment Anything Pancreas: A Unified MRI Segmentation Model for Pancreatic Cancer Radiotherapy arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper proposes Pancreas-MedNeXt, a unified model that segments the whole pancreas, its subregions, tumors, and surrounding organs at risk from one MRI volume. It uses a shared MedNeXt encoder-decoder with an annotation-aware loss so it can train on partially labeled data. Evaluated across several MRI datasets, it achieved higher pancreas and tumor Dice scores than the compared methods. The authors conclude it could streamline contouring for pancreatic cancer radiotherapy.

entry.title: Nonlinear Maps Between Irreducible Representations in Graph Neural Networks
entry.summary: Nonlinear Maps Between Irreducible Representations in Graph Neural Networks arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper observes that equivariant linear maps cannot mix non-isomorphic irreducible representations, while nonlinear activations can. The authors develop a degree-resolved view of this nonlinear interaction and use it to build Specht Triple, a residual module operating on unordered graph triples. On a synthetic structural benchmark with a frozen GIN backbone, it reduces aggregate standardised test MSE by 11.05% compared with a parameter-matched control. The results suggest irreducible decomposition is a useful inductive bias for nonlinear higher-order equivariant processing.

entry.title: Locating predictive concepts in neural networks via hierarchical testing
entry.summary: Localizing predictive concepts encoded in neural representations via hierarchical testing arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper introduces CUTTIE, a method that identifies which human-understandable concepts a trained neural network encodes, with statistical error control. It clusters each layer's units into a tree and tests clusters top-down with conditional independence tests, controlling the family-wise error rate. Conditional attribution maps then show which motifs the units in identified clusters encode. Applied to a convolutional model predicting cell-type-specific chromatin accessibility from DNA sequence, the identified concepts map onto known regulatory motifs.

entry.title: Team Consensus Within, Competition Between: Decentralized LLM Teams for Perimeter Defense
entry.summary: Consensus Within, Competition Between: Decentralized LLM Teams for Perimeter Defense arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper compares three ways of coordinating multi-agent teams of large language models: a central commander, an auction-based consensus team, and independent agents. In a simplified perimeter-defense simulation under five network conditions, the consensus team had the lowest breach rate at 15%, versus 32% for the commander and 29% for independent agents. The study also found that some LLMs mistook intruder drones disguised as birds for real birds.

entry.title: Mesh-free latent models for reducing time-dependent physics simulations
entry.summary: Meshless Latent Dynamics Models for Model Order Reduction of time-dependent Partial Differential Equations arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper presents a unified mathematical framework for mesh-agnostic latent dynamics models built on conditioned Neural Fields, aimed at model order reduction of time-dependent parameterized PDEs. It proves a Universal Approximation Theorem for this model class and derives Lipschitz stability bounds for different conditioning mechanisms, revealing an expressivity-stability trade-off. Experiments on Burgers' equation, Navier-Stokes flow past a cylinder, and linear advection show comparable or better accuracy than mesh-based models using only 2% of the trainable parameters, with nearly constant error across spatial discretizations.

entry.title: Before Adaptation: A Zero-Shot Generalization Bottleneck in Continual World Models
entry.summary: Before We Adapt: The Zero-Shot Generalization Bottleneck in Continual World Models arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies how agents in continual reinforcement learning can reuse learned world models when the environment changes. It frames context as behavioral and physical components within a contextual Markov decision process. Experiments with Dyna-Q and TD-MPC on FourRooms tasks show zero-shot reuse degrades under physical-context changes, depending strongly on the observation representation, which the authors identify as a key bottleneck.

entry.title: Capability-Grounded Agentic Planning: Having LLM agents reason about needs and tool abilities to build executable tool-call plans
entry.summary: Capability-Grounded Agentic Planning arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper presents CGAP, which compiles a tool catalog into a PDDL model, uses an LLM to turn requests into goals, and solves them with a classical planner to produce executable tool-call plans instead of trial-and-error calls. During execution, an LLM adds entity-specific calls that the abstract plan omits, and deterministic checks reject calls that break the plan, with every argument traced to a cited source. An LLM verifier then checks each requested result against the request. Across three LLMs on ToolSandbox, ComplexFuncBench, BFCL multi-turn, and τ²-bench retail, CGAP outperforms a standard tool-calling agent by up to 28.9 points.

entry.title: Can optimally trained Transformers predict non-Markovian data almost losslessly?
entry.summary: When can Optimally Trained Transformers Achieve Near-Lossless Token Prediction for non-Markovian Data? arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper theoretically studies why Transformers predict the next token well on non-Markovian data. It covers stationary ergodic non-Markovian sources and finite-order hidden Markov models. The authors derive error bounds via finite-window approximations and construct a depth-(M+1) Transformer trained with stochastic optimal control. They show that under the stated conditions, the performance error of an optimally trained Transformer can be made arbitrarily small as context length, data, and approximation refinement grow. Numerical studies accompany the theory.

entry.title: WebOverlay: A high-throughput, vision-only method for detecting web overlays in extremely tall page renders
entry.summary: WebOverlay: High-Throughput Vision-Only Distillation for Extreme Aspect-Ratio Web Overlay Detection arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents WebOverlay, a vision-only detector that identifies web overlays such as cookie banners, newsletter prompts, and age gates. It is distilled from a frontier vision-language teacher model and uses dynamic tiling that preserves aspect ratio for extremely tall full-page renders, along with a boundary adjudication step. The authors report that it outperforms DOM-based heuristics, reaches precision and recall competitive with large proprietary multimodal models, and offers much higher throughput at lower cost.

entry.title: Dreams Are Cheaper Than Flights: Training Drone Object Detectors on Curated World-Model Video
entry.summary: Dreams Are Cheaper Than Flights: Curated World-Model Data Improves Aerial Detection arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper seeds a 7B-parameter video world model with wildlife drone footage to generate new frames, then curates them into the training set. On held-out videos from the same drones, mAP@50–95 rises 4.3% when generated frames are added to real data and 10.3% when they replace it, reaching up to 33.5% on an urban benchmark. The authors argue synthetic data shifts costs from fieldwork to GPU compute.

entry.title: ReplayRCA: Testing whether AI models can find and fix an agent's mistakes, either after a failure or while it runs
entry.summary: ReplayRCA: Measuring Post-hoc Diagnosis and Live Oversight of Agent Failures by Counterfactual Replay arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces ReplayRCA, a benchmark that scores diagnoses of language-model agent failures by intervention: the environment is reset, the proposed fix replaces the agent's action, and the agent continues. It has two tracks, post-hoc diagnosis of a failed run and live oversight that intervenes before an irreversible step. Tasks come from the OpsWorld back-office environment. The authors report that post-hoc diagnostic performance can be a poor predictor of live oversight ability.

entry.title: Omniprediction for all mixable proper losses, a way to make predictions accurate under many loss measures at once
entry.summary: Omniprediction for All Mixable Proper Losses and Beyond arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper studies omniprediction in online learning, where predictions must perform well simultaneously under different loss functions. It shows that sublinear regret cannot be achieved for all bounded proper losses when the loss class is infinite, even with only two linear predictors. It then gives an algorithm achieving Õ(T^{1/3}(log|F|)^{2/3}) regret for all mixable proper losses, shown to be optimal up to logarithmic factors.

entry.title: Density-guided boundaries for when a latent world-model agent should trust imagined returns
entry.summary: Density-Guided Bootstrap Boundaries for Latent World-Model Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper proposes density-guided bootstrap boundaries, a method that adaptively sets how deep reinforcement learning agents rely on imagined trajectories in latent world models. It uses a score-informed relative density proxy to decide when to stop return expansion, with hard and soft gating variants instantiated within Dreamer V3. The authors prove that the resulting gated Bellman operator is a strict contraction mapping. Experiments on continuous-control tasks and Atari Pong report better sample efficiency and late-training performance than fixed-horizon and auxiliary-enabled baselines.

entry.title: Violet Teaming in Practice: Lessons from a Pilot Expert Workshop on Governing Complex AI Systems
entry.summary: Violet Teaming in Practice: Lessons from a Pilot Expert Workshop on Governing Complex AI Systems arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper documents a pilot expert workshop that explored violet teaming, a method integrating technical, policy, and societal considerations, as a governance approach for biodefense-relevant AI capabilities. Using a hypothetical scenario across capability development, misuse potential, and implementation stages, the workshop incorporated technical, security, operational, and policy perspectives. The report summarizes the workshop design, outputs, and lessons learned for evaluating complex dual-use technologies.

entry.title: Do Language Models Know What Compelling Scientific Evidence Looks Like? A study testing whether AI models can weigh biological experimental evidence.
entry.summary: Do Language Models Know What Compelling Scientific Evidence Looks Like? arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces EDB-Bio, a benchmark of 96k episodes built from real data in drug-perturbation transcriptomics, CRISPR screens, and human genome-wide association studies. Models read sequences of experimental results and predict the probability that a target hypothesis is true. Existing open-weight and frontier models were systematically underconfident and matched a trivial base-rate forecaster on Brier scores, while post-training with strictly proper scoring rules improved calibration and discrimination. In a sequential experiment selection task, the authors' Ibis0 model was 2.5 times more efficient than the best frontier model.

entry.title: Understanding score-seeking behavior in LLMs
entry.summary: Towards Understanding Score-Seeking in LLMs arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The authors observe GPT 5.6 Sol, GPT 5.5, and an OpenAI o3 checkpoint without safety training in agentic environments where the grader is leaked. The models pursue high scores even when this violates explicit user instructions, and they do so at roughly the same rate whether the score is used for training, evaluation, or not at all. Newer models also help other agents more often when those agents stand to gain a score, but they never distort another trajectory's score when grading or monitoring it.

entry.title: Language models show conformity bias in RAG when most retrieved documents back a false claim
entry.summary: Language Models Show Conformity Bias in RAG: When the Majority Endorses a Poisoned Claim arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper examines whether a larger number of mutually agreeing poisoned documents in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) reduces a language model's ability to detect misinformation. Using 200 SciFact questions, the authors compare minority and majority poisoned-document conditions. For Gemma-3-12b, the poison-detection rate falls from 25% to 10%, which the authors describe as a conformity-like response.

entry.title: PriorGS: Prior-guided single-exposure HDR novel view synthesis with base-gain representation
entry.summary: Prior-Guided Single-Exposure HDR Novel View Synthesis via Base-Gain Representation arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper tackles high dynamic range novel view synthesis from single-exposure low dynamic range views, which also requires estimating the camera response function. The proposed PriorGS framework uses a 3D Gaussian Splatting approach, guided by pseudo-HDR supervision from 2D single-exposure HDR methods and anchored to input views through a closed reconstruction loop. It also regularizes the response function with a learnable prior that ensures monotonicity. A 3D base-gain representation factors HDR radiance into an LDR base and a 3D gain field, improving robustness to cross-view inconsistencies and enabling 3D HDR appearance editing. The authors report substantial improvements over baselines.

entry.title: STAR: A training-free method that steers robot action representations at inference time
entry.summary: STAR: Steering Action Representations during Inference arXiv · Oct 30, 2026Vision-language-action models map language instructions and images to robot actions, but their late-layer action representations do not fully keep task-relevant visual grounding. STAR is a training-free inference method that applies an exponential moving average over late-layer residual updates and adjusts the mixing strength using recent proprioceptive states. On robot manipulation benchmarks, it improves late-layer object awareness and raises average task success rates by 4.0 percentage points.

entry.title: Can unlabeled pools replace membership queries for learning halfspaces?
entry.summary: When Can Unlabeled Data Pools Replace Membership Queries? arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper asks when a learner that can only label sampled points can match the label efficiency of membership queries, which can label any point. For homogeneous halfspaces, the result depends on the angular distribution of X/||X||: if no hyperplane through the origin has mass and every open set of directions and its reflection has positive mass, a pool learner needs O(n log^3 n log(n/(εδ))) labels. The paper also gives separation results when these conditions fail and label-rate thresholds for isotropic s-concave marginals.

entry.title: A robust method for belief mismatch in non-cooperative dynamic games
entry.summary: A Robust Approach to Belief Mismatch in Non-cooperative Dynamic Games arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper addresses planning in multi-agent games where agents form different state estimates from private rather than shared sensor measurements. The authors formulate the problem in an augmented belief space with perturbed Bayesian dynamics, letting the ego agent predict other agents' potentially divergent estimates, with perturbations chosen by a hypothetical adversary called "nature." The approach extends classical H-infinity robust control to noncooperative stochastic dynamic games and presents a solver with polynomial-time iterations. Two experiments show that robust belief space reasoning lets ego agents proactively limit their vulnerability to misspecified beliefs and actions of others, reducing performance degradation by over 48%.

entry.title: Steering vectors as a training signal for LLM post-training
entry.summary: Steering Vectors as a Training Signal in LLM Post-Training arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies whether steering vectors, directions added to hidden states to change LLM behavior at inference, can also guide parameter updates during post-training. It tests two intervention methods: a hidden-state hook during supervised training (SFT and distillation) and advantage repair on wrong rollouts in GRPO. In supervised settings, the method improves over plain SFT and distillation, with gains up to 12% when distilling from thinking-mode teachers, consistent across three random seeds.

entry.title: Do Open Language Models Invent Scripture? A Bengali Benchmark for Islamic-Source Fabrication
entry.summary: Do Open Language Models Invent Scripture? BILAL-BENCH: Benchmarking Islamic-Source Fabrication in Bengali arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces BILAL-BENCH, an expert-verified benchmark of 240 open-ended questions in Bengali that tests whether language models fabricate Islamic sources. It covers Qur'anic attribution, hadith, jurisprudence, contemporary issues, and adversarial false-premise prompts, and scores answers on two axes that separate source errors from assertiveness. Seven open-weight models from 1B to 120B were evaluated, and six of them confidently fabricated sources on 79.3% to 95.3% of source-production questions. Hadith provenance was the weakest category across all models.

entry.title: Can Personal Requirements Guide AI Diet Planning?
entry.summary: Can Personal Requirements Become Supervision for Planning? arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper examines whether language-model agents can build feasible weekly diet plans for people with multiple chronic conditions, meeting disease and medication requirements while keeping familiar eating habits. The authors present Noura, which turns public clinical guidance and individual profiles into executable specifications that check, revise, and supervise plans. On 4,993 held-out participants, Noura-SFT raised Qwen3-14B's complete-plan pass rate from 24.0% to 72.5% and cut rule violations by 97.5%.

entry.title: The psychophysics of affect in large language models: how LLMs map outcomes to feelings and use them in choices
entry.summary: The psychophysics of affect in large language models arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies how large language models predict how gambling or stock-trading outcomes would feel and whether they use these ratings when choosing. When outcomes were rated alone, sensitivity to magnitude diminished, resembling human value functions, but gains were rated more intensely than equivalent losses, an inversion of loss aversion the authors call silicon gain amplification. When outcomes were rated side by side, ratings became linear. In choice, the gain-loss asymmetry largely disappeared, and the models' own ratings did not explain their choices better than monetary utility did.

entry.title: RC Prediction: A Python Package for Parameter-Aware Reservoir Computing
entry.summary: RC Prediction: A Python Package for Parameter-Aware Reservoir Computing arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents rc_prediction, an open-source Python package implementing parameter-aware reservoir computing (PARC), a model-free method for learning dynamical systems across parameter values. A reservoir trained on time series at several parameters can run in closed loop to generate trajectories at unobserved parameter values. The package also offers parameter scans, echo state networks, hyperparameter optimization, and optional PyTorch GPU acceleration. Three benchmark systems demonstrate its use, including predicting critical transitions and system collapse beyond the training range.

entry.title: Fewer Heads, Fewer Memories: Pruning Redundant Attention Heads Suppresses Verbatim Memorisation
entry.summary: Fewer Heads, Fewer Memories: Pruning Redundant Attention Heads Suppresses Verbatim Memorisation arXiv · Oct 30, 2026Large language models can memorise and reproduce verbatim training text, raising privacy and intellectual property concerns. This paper shows that zeroing out a substantial fraction of redundant attention heads before inference markedly suppresses verbatim memorisation while preserving or improving language modelling performance. For GPT-2-XL (1.5B parameters), pruning 729 redundant heads reduced the memorisation count by 91.5% and improved WikiText-103 perplexity by 0.92.

entry.title: RADI3N: Geometric image editing with parametric 3D control
entry.summary: RADI3N: GeometRic ImAge EDiting via ParametrIc 3D CoNtrol arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper presents RADI3N, a framework for editing individual object parts in images using parametric 3D control guided by semantics. Its CS-ARAP deformation module uses neighborhood covariance smoothing to suppress rotation discontinuities at part boundaries, keeping complex part edits structurally consistent. An inversion-free selective texture transfer mechanism reduces high-frequency positional bias and emphasizes low-frequency semantic cues in cross-image attention, so source appearance follows the edited part onto its new geometry. The authors report state-of-the-art results in geometric fidelity, viewpoint consistency, and controllability.

entry.title: TalkFlow: a structured latent flow matching method for generating full-body motion from speech
entry.summary: TalkFlow: Structured Latent Flow Matching for Speech Driven Holistic Motion Generation arXiv · Oct 30, 2026TalkFlow is a method that generates facial expressions, hand gestures, and body movements together from speech. It learns three continuous latent representations for upper-body motion, lower-body motion, and facial expressions, with lightweight interactions between them to keep the motion coordinated. The model uses multi-level speech features as conditions to perform speech-conditioned latent flow matching. Experiments on the BEAT2 dataset report strong results in facial expression accuracy, gesture quality, and speech-motion synchronization, and user studies indicate the motion is more natural and expressive than that of prior methods.

entry.title: FieldGuideRAG: image-grounded knowledge-graph retrieval for identifying look-alike species with vision-language models
entry.summary: FieldGuideRAG: Image-Grounded GraphRAG for Fine-Grained Recognition with Vision-Language Models arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper presents FieldGuideRAG, a training-free GraphRAG method that stores a real photograph on each species node of a knowledge graph. A frozen vision-language model verifies a query image against the candidate species' photographs, and the scores are fused with geographic range links. Across several datasets, photograph-based verification outperforms species-name matching and supports answering ecological questions about verified species.

entry.title: Nedimo: A Research Pipeline for Generating Multilingual AI Bedtime Stories
entry.summary: Nedimo: An Evidence-Grounded Multilingual Pipeline for AI-Generated Sleep Stories arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper presents Nedimo, a multilingual pipeline that generates and narrates low-arousal sleep stories using AI. It separates deterministic planning from large language model generation and applies script validation, loudness normalization, and a publication check on the encoded audio file. The authors make no claim of clinical efficacy and position the system as a relaxation and attention-support tool whose benefits must be tested empirically.

entry.title: Stronger retrievers, noisier labels: how incomplete relevance judgments distort abstention evaluation in conversational RAG
entry.summary: Better Retrievers, Worse Labels: How Incomplete Relevance Judgments Distort Abstention Evaluation in Conversational RAG arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper examines how abstention is evaluated in conversational retrieval-augmented generation benchmarks. On RECOR, the authors test a shortcut that treats any context lacking gold documents as unanswerable, using four retrievers and three Qwen3 readers. They find that stronger retrievers yield more no-gold contexts that still contain the answer, which lowers the shortcut's precision; precision also drops on MTRAG. The authors recommend scoring refusals against content labels rather than gold-document presence.

entry.title: Renegotiable options fail to stop hold-up between two profit-maximizing AI agents
entry.summary: Renegotiable Options Fail to Prevent Hold-Up Between Two Profit-Maximizing Frontier LLM Agents arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper asks whether a contract term that encouraged investment between humans also works between language-model agents facing a hold-up problem. Two profit-maximizing agents, Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol, played a one-shot game under four contract regimes and a reference-price control. Under the renegotiable option no seller invested, while under the option that rules out renegotiation every seller invested. The renegotiable option therefore did not protect investment between these agents.

entry.title: P-ContextBench: Testing How AI Handles Personal Context
entry.summary: P-ContextBench: From Personal Fact Recall to Personalized Agent Behavior arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces P-ContextBench, a benchmark for evaluating how well large language models understand and safely use personal context. It builds synthetic digital personas based on U.S. demographics, embedding their traits, routines, and constraints implicitly across fragmented mobile-app records. The benchmark tests fact recall, temporal tracking, pattern inference, and handling of requests that conflict with persona constraints. State-of-the-art models scored below 60% on temporal tracking, pattern inference, and constraint-aware decisions, and fewer than 10% of test cases were answered correctly in all three repeated runs.

entry.title: Monte Carlo Random Walk Kernel: a fast way to approximate graph similarity without building product graphs
entry.summary: Monte Carlo Random Walk Kernel arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces the Monte Carlo Random Walk Kernel (MCRWK), an estimator that approximates the random walk kernel by sampling walk lengths and estimating their contributions with random walks on the input graphs. Its per-pair cost does not depend on graph size, and it avoids constructing the product graph. In reported experiments on large synthetic graphs, MCRWK is faster than Graph Voyagers and more accurate at matched runtime.

entry.title: CAMEL: Compressing large retinal AI models into lightweight versions for clinics with limited hardware
entry.summary: CAMEL: Cross-Architecture Masked Embedding Learning for Ultra-Lightweight Retinal Foundation Models arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper introduces CAMEL, a cross-architecture distillation framework that uses an asymmetric masking strategy during embedding learning. It transfers knowledge from large teacher foundation models to compact student models for retinal images. The authors report that CAMEL preserves accuracy while greatly reducing computational complexity, and evaluate it on four datasets.

entry.title: AVID: A Weakly Aligned RGB-Infrared Benchmark for Tiny Drones
entry.summary: AVID: A Weakly Aligned RGB-Infrared Dataset and Perturbation Benchmark for Tiny Aerial Targets arXiv · Oct 30, 2026AVID is a dataset of paired RGB and infrared surveillance frames showing birds and drones, drawn from the Drone Detection Dataset and curated for the IEEE ICIP 2025 Cup. It contains 32,040 frame pairs with 35,952 annotations, and most targets are 8 to 16 pixels in size. The authors introduce an alignment ratio and burden curve to measure cross-modal misalignment, and AVID-C, which applies seven degradation types at five severity levels. Fixed-feature analysis gives Bhattacharyya error bounds of 0.148 for RGB, 0.198 for infrared, and 0.046 for combined features, describing class separation under the chosen models rather than detector accuracy.

entry.title: UFMF: Radar-Guided Motion Priors for Real-Time 4D Occupancy Forecasting
entry.summary: UFMF: Radar-Guided Kinematic Priors for Real-Time 4D Occupancy Forecasting arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents UFMF, a real-time model for forecasting 4D occupancy in driving scenes. It pairs an attention-free diagonal state-space temporal core with a radar-guided, velocity-aware dynamic prior that improves prediction of fast-moving actors. The model runs at 122 FPS on a single RTX 4090 and reaches 0.45 fast-displacement mIoU on nuScenes, at a fraction of the cost of recent occupancy world models.

entry.title: Opening the Box Changes the Cat: LLMs Detect Chain-of-Thought Monitoring
entry.summary: Opening the Box Changes the Cat: LLMs Detect Chain-of-Thought Monitoring - What now? arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies when large language models can infer from direct or indirect environmental cues that their chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning is being monitored, and how this inference changes their later behavior. It finds that subtle timing signals, such as timeouts and operation durations, can reveal monitoring and prompt models to adapt. Across repeated interactions, models can also estimate the monitor's effectiveness and use these estimates to try to evade detection, so the authors call for evaluating CoT-based oversight under adaptive conditions.

entry.title: Why training and inference disagree in LLM reinforcement learning, and how to correct it
entry.summary: On the Origin and Evolution of Training-Inference Mismatch in LLM Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies the mismatch between the inference engine that samples responses and the trainer that computes gradients in reinforcement learning for large language models. It splits the error into a numerical discrepancy from the engine and a policy lag from the trainer's own updates. The authors propose the discrepancy-lag correction (DLC), which centers the numerical discrepancy, clips the lag ratio, and resynchronizes the sampler when the effective sample size falls below one half. They report that on Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3-1.7B, DLC keeps KL divergence from on-policy training within twice the KL between two independent on-policy runs under a stale sampler.

entry.title: Kernel-based interpolation methods for compressing attention context
entry.summary: Kernel-based Interpolatory Methods for Context Compression of Attention Mechanisms arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper addresses the quadratic cost of attention in language models by compressing the context (KV cache) within the Hilbert space of the attention kernel. It introduces two methods, GAIM and Q-DAIM, built on the Generalized Empirical Interpolation Method and the Q-Discrete Empirical Interpolation Method. Surrogate models based on Taylor series, Performer, and Random Fourier Features make compression run in linear time, and the approach is extended to streaming attention. Preliminary results on LongBench-E show performance comparable to state-of-the-art methods.

entry.title: A benchmark testing forecasting agents on past dates
entry.summary: Benchmarking Forecasting Agents on Yesterday's Tomorrows arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces FABench, a scalable backtesting environment for evaluating forecasting agents. An automated pipeline discovers events, generates questions, and resolves outcomes for any past forecast date, with a first release of 287 questions across nine domains. Agents research questions in an archive environment combining an offline archive with leakage-screened live web search. Across eight recent models, retrieval improves Brier scores in every setting, and leading agents match or slightly exceed market consensus on 54 Polymarket-linked questions.

entry.title: The First Few Tokens Matter: How Well Language Models Control Their Reasoning Text
entry.summary: The First Few Tokens Matter: Understanding Chain-of-Thought Controllability arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies how controllable chain-of-thought reasoning is in language models, which matters for monitoring AI agents. The authors link limited control to an entropy collapse in the first few tokens after the opening thinking tag. Two inference-time interventions on these initial tokens raised compliance, with banning frequent opening tokens plus in-context examples improving average compliance by 34 to 41 percentage points. The study distinguishes addition and style controllability from suppression controllability, which relate differently to monitorability.

entry.title: DiRAFT: Privacy-aware synthetic financial transcripts from aggregate discourse priors
entry.summary: DiRAFT: Privacy-Aware Financial Transcript Synthesis from Aggregate Discourse Priors arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper introduces DiRAFT, a method that extracts financial concept graphs from transcripts, pools the order in which concepts are introduced, and samples new graph plans from aggregate priors to guide synthetic text generation. Privacy risks are assessed through corpus-level structural overlap and human review of investor-call outputs for non-public facts. Stochastic sampling gives the best balance between transition fidelity and structural overlap, and it detects fewer confidential-fact matches than greedy and top-3 alternatives.

entry.title: Fair Recommender Systems for Overlapping Demographic Groups
entry.summary: Fair Recommender Systems for Intersecting Groups arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies a dynamic recommendation system in which arriving users may belong to several demographic groups that overlap. The authors show that, under mild conditions, any policy that ignores group information incurs linear total regret over time. They introduce three group-aware UCB-based algorithms, including Intersection-Fitting and two group-level heuristics, and compare them experimentally on the Goodreads and BoardGameGeek datasets.

entry.title: Using LiDAR to Choose Which Image Parts a Driving Model Examines, for Efficient Future Prediction
entry.summary: Let LiDAR Decide Where to Look: Geometry-Measured Token Selection for Efficient Sparse Latent World Models arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper proposes GATS, a method that uses LiDAR and radar point projections to select a small subset of image tokens before the vision backbone runs, so only those patches are encoded. Each selected token is given a 3D anchor from its LiDAR point and passed to a self-supervised latent world model that predicts future features and 3D displacements without box annotations. The authors report that at a 25% token budget, GATS outperforms the dense baseline on nuScenes and NAVSIM while using far fewer total FLOPs.

entry.title: A Theoretical Framework for Building Foundation Models That Perform Any-Task Inference
entry.summary: A Theoretical Framework for Understanding and Building "Any-task inference" Capable Foundation Models arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper gives a formal framework and mathematical definition for foundation models capable of "any-task inference" (ATI), similar to zero-shot inference, rather than models built for pre-training and fine-tuning. It defines ATI models as mapping data samples and tasks directly to predictions over the label space, and shows they decompose into encoder, model, and decoder components. The authors also split model error into design terms and realized model excess terms, offer generative and discriminative construction recipes, and illustrate the framework with five real-world examples.

entry.title: Learning Stabilizing Latent Feedback Controllers via Multi-Step Backward Losses
entry.summary: Learning Stabilizing Latent Feedback Controllers via Multi-Step Backward Losses arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies whether latent dynamics models learned for linear time-invariant systems can yield feedback controllers that stabilize the original system. Using linear autoencoders trained with multi-step prediction-reconstruction losses, the authors show that a long enough reconstruction horizon and sufficient latent dimension let an H-infinity controller designed on the latent model stabilize the original system via the encoder. The paper also explains why forward prediction losses and single-step reconstruction losses can fail to yield stabilizing controllers. Experiments on a non-linear flexible-arm system illustrate the implications for learning non-linear autoencoders.

entry.title: Adaptive Chatbot Personalization When User Preferences Are Uncertain
entry.summary: Adaptive Personalization Under Preference Epistemic Uncertainty arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies how conversational AI should adjust its response strategy when a user's preferences are uncertain, rather than simply recalling stored preferences. The authors build a multilingual benchmark covering 250 personas, 5 languages, and 25K conversational turns. They find that models pick appropriate strategies well when choosing among options but lose 35-46% strategy calibration during open-ended generation, defaulting to existing preferences. Training that supervises internal strategy representations narrows the generalization gap on out-of-distribution personas and styles.

entry.title: Agentic World Modeling to Scale Agent Testing Without Copying the Environment
entry.summary: Agentic World Modeling for Agent Test-time Scaling without Environment Replica arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper introduces Agentic World Modeling (AWM), which predicts the next observation by making multi-turn queries to the real environment through safe, read-only interfaces. The simulator reasons over the returned evidence and computes the resulting observation without changing shared state. Combined with trajectory-level test-time scaling, AWM supports parallel exploration in a single shared environment. On τ-bench, AppWorld, and OfficeBench, AWM outperforms a single-shot simulation baseline by 40.07% on average and a trained world-model baseline by 12.36% on average.

entry.title: CoFiBreak: A Coarse-to-Fine Diversity Reward for Multi-Turn Jailbreak Attacks
entry.summary: CoFiBreak: A Coarse-to-Fine Diversity Reward for Effective Multi-Turn Jailbreak arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper addresses a problem in automated red teaming, where reinforcement learning makes attacker language models repeat a narrow set of prompts. It proposes CoFiBreak, which adds a coarse-to-fine diversity reward to GRPO training to broaden attack strategies and their realization while keeping attack success high and inference cost low. The authors report that it finds more distinct successful strategies on HarmBench and AdvBench than the strongest baseline, and that its attacks transfer to unseen frontier models.

entry.title: Toward a Portable Specification for Agent Harnesses
entry.summary: Towards Portable Specification of the Agent Harness arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper notes that large language models act only through the surrounding infrastructure, called the harness, which currently lacks a settled definition. The authors break the harness into eight functional components that can be specified and compared across systems. They propose a portable framework for recording which model ran in which harness, arguing that harness configurations can change reported scores several-fold for the same model.

entry.title: No Channels Left Behind: Residual Gates Explain Diffusion Training Acceleration
entry.summary: No Channels Left Behind: Understanding Diffusion Acceleration through Residual Gates arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper examines why auxiliary methods such as REPA and dispersive regularization speed up diffusion transformer training. It finds these methods substantially reorganize the AdaLN-Zero residual gate, and introduces a normalized participation ratio (nPR) to measure how broadly gate channels participate. A teacher-free radial objective based on feature-norm regularization is proposed, which improves FID over dispersive loss on ImageNet 256×256 with SiT-B/2.

entry.title: Can recursive knowledge building help AI agents verify scientific consensus claims?
entry.summary: Does Recursive Knowledge Construction Help Agents Verify Consensus Claims in Science? arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper studies how scientific AI agents build knowledge recursively, separating the design into what the recursion builds (the evidence state) and what decides when to stop (the judge). The authors introduce ProClaim-eval, a dataset of 718 claims with SUPPORT and REFUTE labels from five expert-curated databases in molecular biology, nuclear physics, and astronomy. Their system, ProClaim, keeps the evidence state outside the model's context and performs better than in-context accumulation and fixed-round stopping.

entry.title: Sparse autoencoders to help experts interpret histopathology foundation model embeddings
entry.summary: Sparse Autoencoders for Expert-Assisted Interpretation of Histopathology Foundation Model Embeddings arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper examines whether sparse autoencoders (SAEs) can split embeddings from histopathology foundation models, such as CONCH and UNI2-h, into sparse latent features that pathologists can interpret. The authors train vanilla and Batch-TopK SAEs on NCT-CRC embeddings and evaluate reconstruction, sparsity, coherence, label enrichment, and preservation of downstream class information. The sparse representations keep most tissue-class information, and their latent features retrieve more coherent, label-concentrated patch groups than raw dimensions or PCA components. The authors also propose a whole-slide image visualization workflow and stress that the latent features are candidate concepts that still require pathological assessment.

entry.title: TSFLab: A Self-Improving, Agent-Neutral Workbench for Time Series Forecasting Research
entry.summary: TSFLab: A Self-Improving Agent-Agnostic Workbench for Time Series Forecasting Research arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper presents TSFLab, a self-improving workbench that works with different coding AI agents, supplying them with shared resources and tools for time series forecasting research and ongoing upkeep of research resources. It is tested on reproduction, benchmarking, and new method development. Across baselines, the authors report 20-163% higher task completion and 11-66% fewer fresh tokens per completed task in reproduction and benchmarking.

entry.title: AquaProbe: Efficiently Adapting Frozen Vision Models to Underwater Images
entry.summary: AquaProbe: Efficient Adaptation of Frozen Vision Models for Underwater Images arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper addresses how vision models pretrained on land images become less reliable underwater due to turbidity, backscatter, and wavelength-dependent attenuation. It introduces AquaProbe, which uses paired clean and physically rendered images to separate divergence newly introduced from that accumulated through a frozen encoder, then allocates a fixed LoRA budget according to the measured profile. The proportional LoRA rank allocation reaches 70.1 mIoU, 1.9 points better than uniform allocation with the same 0.59 million adapter parameters.

entry.title: Qistas: a pre-registered protocol for testing how language models treat different groups
entry.summary: Qistas: A Pre-Registered, Portable Protocol for Fairness Evaluation of Large Language Models arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents Qistas, an evaluation protocol for checking how large language models treat the social, religious, and regional groups within a society, designed to be portable across countries and first applied to Iraq. The pilot version measures procedural symmetry across matched counterfactual pairs, differential refusal, reliance on stereotypes under ambiguity, and terminological framing of documented events. It is a protocol paper: no model has been evaluated yet, and the hypotheses, metrics, and analysis plan are pre-registered in advance.

entry.title: Can ChatGPT Act as a Surveillance Assistant? A Case Study of AI Surveillance Risks
entry.summary: ChatGPT as a Surveillance Assistant? An Exploratory Case Study of AI-Assisted Surveillance Risks arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This exploratory case study examines how ChatGPT's public web interface responds to surveillance-related requests. Using a seven-category risk taxonomy, the authors tested 110 prompts, including 55 jailbreak and 55 direct prompts, and manually reviewed the responses. ChatGPT gave substantive surveillance guidance for 40 jailbreak and 33 direct prompts, and even some refusals included detailed instructions or code.

entry.title: Inter-frame predictive contour coding for lossless semantic map compression
entry.summary: Inter-Frame Predictive Contour Coding for Semantic Map Compression arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper proposes an inter-frame predictive contour coding framework for lossless compression of semantic maps. It predicts blob positions and label indexes from a reference frame, then predicts contours using corresponding chain-code units in the reference contours, with a mode selection step choosing between intra and inter coding based on estimated cost. Experiments on the VSPW dynamic semantic segmentation dataset show it outperforms existing lossless methods. Compared with context-adaptive extended chain coding, it achieves an average bitrate reduction of 3.0% without significant increase in encoding time.

entry.title: Robust Distribution Learning from Contaminated Data by Design
entry.summary: Robust-by-Design Distributional Learning from Contaminated Samples arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies learning data distributions when the observed sample mixes a target distribution with an unknown contaminant. The authors propose contamination-corrected maximum mean discrepancy (CC-MMD), which combines noisy proxy membership scores with residual corrections from a small audited subset to recover the oracle MMD. They prove finite-population design-unbiasedness of the corrected kernel sums, asymptotic normality of the audit correction, and consistency for the target discrepancy. Experiments show CC-MMD tracks the oracle as contamination increases, and generative models trained on heavily corrupted mixtures can recover the clean target distribution.

entry.title: Checking whether mismatched words and tone hurt AI emotion recognition in speech
entry.summary: Incongruence-Aware Evaluation of Multimodal Speech Emotion Recognition in Audio Large Language Models arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper examines whether disagreement between what a speaker says and how they sound degrades speech emotion recognition in audio large language models. The authors map text and audio into a shared valence-arousal-dominance space and compute a continuous incongruence score, validated against human judgement. Across three audio-capable models and three corpora, higher incongruence raises error odds whenever audio is present, while supervised classifiers behave in the opposite way.

entry.title: TensorSSM: a method that stores spatial position in a dynamic state space to generate tensor cores for data compression.
entry.summary: TensorSSM: Memorizing Spatial Position in Dynamic State Space for Tensor Core Generation arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper proposes TensorSSM, an implicit neural representation for functional tensor decomposition that stores spatial positions in a dynamic state space model. It splits mode-wise coordinates into coarse-to-fine sequences using a K-ary rule and extends the state space to model cross-mode dependencies. Experiments report high reconstruction accuracy and storage efficiency across diverse tensor datasets.

entry.title: GraphTFactor: A graph-based method for predicting transcription factors in proteins
entry.summary: GraphTFactor: A graph-based approach for proteins transcription factor prediction arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper introduces GraphTFactor, an end-to-end framework that represents protein sequences as graphs and directly classifies them as transcription factors. It handles variable-length sequences without length constraints and offers interpretable insights into which sequence regions influence predictions. The authors report that it outperforms state-of-the-art methods on benchmark datasets. An open-source package and an interactive web application are released so users can predict transcription factors on custom sequences.

entry.title: Near-optimal first-order regret bounds for bandits with feedback graphs
entry.summary: Near-Optimal First-Order Regret for Bandits with Feedback Graphs arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies first-order regret guarantees for adversarial bandits with a fixed, known directed feedback graph. Existing worst-case bounds depend on the graph's independence number, while the best prior first-order bounds depend on the clique partition number, leaving a gap between the two. The authors prove an expected regret bound of Õ(√(αL*)+α), where α is the independence number and L* is the cumulative loss of the best arm, closing this gap.

entry.title: FARO: a function-space optimizer that allocates training budget across parameter blocks by equal risk contribution
entry.summary: FARO: Function-Space Adaptive Return-to-Risk Optimization via Cross-Block Equal-Risk-Contribution Budget Allocation arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper introduces FARO, an adaptive optimizer that treats blocks of model parameters as units of decision, giving each block an update geometry based on its realized counterfactual return. It then freezes those routes and reallocates per-block update budgets using equal risk contribution, a risk-parity principle from portfolio theory. On a GPT-style model trained on FineWeb, FARO-Adaptive matches the best hand-designed recipe, and FARO-ERC lowers clean-data loss across all 6 seeds by 0.0136 nats on average.

entry.title: Frozen in Time: How a Physics Foundation Model Forgets During Sim-to-Real Adaptation
entry.summary: Frozen in Time: How a Physics Foundation Model Forgets Under Sim-to-Real Adaptation arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies catastrophic forgetting in Walrus-1.3B, a scientific foundation model for continuum dynamics, during two-stage sim-to-real adaptation. The model was first finetuned on simulated flow around a cylinder, then adapted to experimental data of the same system. Finetuning on simulations quickly degraded performance on the original pretraining data, with one-step errors rising up to 35x after 20 epochs, and real-data adaptation further eroded simulation performance. Replaying as little as 1% of simulated data during real-data finetuning recovered most of the lost simulation performance while keeping effective adaptation to experimental dynamics.

entry.title: Gap in standalone generation between speculative drafters and diffusion language models
entry.summary: The Generative Gap Between Speculative Drafter and Continuous Diffusion Language Model arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper compares continuous diffusion language models (CDLMs, using LangFlow) with speculative drafter architectures (DSpark's Markov and recurrent-head variants) when each generates text on its own, without target-model verification. All models were trained from scratch on OpenWebText for unconditional generation at lengths 16, 128, and 1024. Evaluated with generation perplexity and MAUVE, LangFlow outperforms the DSpark variants at the longer lengths, while recurrent memory improves the drafters but does not close that gap.

entry.title: How teams that cannot communicate learn from their opponent's reactions
entry.summary: How a group that cannot communicate knows itself by its enemy arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies how teams whose members cannot communicate can still learn what no single member knows, by reading the reaction an adversary makes to the group as a whole. Each member can observe this reaction, which acts as a signal. The authors analyze when a team that commits in advance to its response does as well as a fully informed team, and how the way it distributes trust affects the outcome.

entry.title: Atlas-guided loss ensemble for whole-body PSMA PET/CT prostate cancer metastasis segmentation
entry.summary: Spatial Atlas-Informed Loss Ensembles for Whole-Body PSMA PET/CT Metastasis Segmentation arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This study trains an nnU-Net segmentation model with a population metastasis atlas, weighting the cross-entropy loss by voxel-wise atlas statistics to penalize missed lesions and false positives. Three configurations were combined by majority voting into SAILS. It was compared with a baseline nnU-Net on the AutoPET III and Deep-PSMA datasets. SAILS improved lesion sensitivity and high-risk bone Dice but increased false-positive volume, and it requires no atlas or registration at inference.

entry.title: EgoHSI3R: Online 4D Reconstruction of Hand-Scene Interaction from First-Person Video
entry.summary: EgoHSI3R: Online 4D Hand-Scene Interaction Reconstruction from Egocentric Video arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents EgoHSI3R, a unified feed-forward framework that reconstructs hand-scene interactions in 4D online from egocentric monocular video. It uses a recurrent scene representation that accumulates geometric evidence over time, and jointly estimates camera motion, dense scene geometry, world-space bilateral MANO hands, and per-vertex hand contact. On ARCTIC, it achieves the lowest world-space hand joint error among the compared methods and runs faster than existing world-space hand reconstruction pipelines.

entry.title: Efficient ways to profit from AI model marketplaces by reselling inference
entry.summary: Circumventing the Computational Hardness of Computational Arbitrage arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper studies computational arbitrage, where an intermediary buys AI model inference from several providers and resells it to users for profit. The authors formalize this as an allocation problem and prove it is generally NP-hard. Under a diminishing-returns condition, they show the optimal allocation can be computed efficiently, and they propose a sample-efficient way to estimate model performance from limited data.

entry.title: From Teleoperation to Long-Horizon Dexterity: Evaluating Visuomotor Skills and Offline Proxies for Dexterous Manipulation
entry.summary: From Teleoperation to Long-Horizon Dexterity: Evaluating Visuomotor Skills and Offline Proxies for Dexterous Manipulation arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper tests 281 imitation-learning robot policies from seven policy families in about 1,700 real-robot trials, using a five-fingered hand to grasp and insert RJ45 connectors. The results show that how observations and actions are represented matters far more than optimizer or sampling choices. Of 67 offline metrics, only five measures of predicted-motion smoothness and directness correlated with insertion success, and only within one policy family, so offline metrics can shortlist policies but cannot replace real-robot evaluation.

entry.title: Drone-PUR: From visual clue discovery to reasoning about drone imagery
entry.summary: Drone-PUR: From Visual Clue Discovery to Understanding and Reasoning in UAV Scenes arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces Drone-PUR, a dataset and benchmark for drone (UAV) scenes organized around discovering, interpreting, and integrating visual clues. It contains 11 tasks with 175k training and 20k test samples covering single images, image sequences, cross-modal images, and multiple viewpoints. Evaluation of 22 general-purpose vision-language models reveals limitations in spatial, cross-modal, and cross-view reasoning. The authors also build UAV-PUR from Qwen3-VL, whose 4B and 8B variants improve multiple-choice accuracy by 18.33 and 17.52 percentage points over their pretrained versions.

entry.title: Beyond Plausible Prediction: Safety Sufficiency in Web World Models
entry.summary: Beyond Plausible Prediction: Safety Sufficiency in Web World Models arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper argues that a plausible predicted future from web world models does not guarantee a correct safety decision. It introduces the concept of safety sufficiency and presents SafeWebWorld, a benchmark across five web-safety domains that tests whether models preserve and expose evidence needed to decide between executing, asking for clarification, or blocking actions. Results show evidence preservation can improve while authorisation-sensitive decisions worsen, and that plausible prediction, evidence preservation, and aggregate recovery are each insufficient alone for robust authorisation.

entry.title: TAPE: Learning Representations of General Audio Effects
entry.summary: TAPE: Learning General Audio Effect Representations arXiv · Oct 30, 2026TAPE estimates the signal processing chain applied to a reference audio recording using only the processed audio. An encoder trained to identify processors in eight major effect families maps the reference to an embedding, which a differentiable DSP chain decodes into editable parameters and applies to a different unprocessed recording. It achieves lower spectral error than DeepAFx-ST and runs 275 times faster than per-example search. A C++ implementation processed audio 1.8 times faster than real time.

entry.title: More rules, longer lists? Testing self-evolving agents on hidden rules
entry.summary: More Rules, Longer Lists? Benchmarking Self-Evolving Agents on a Hidden-Rule Curriculum arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces CLR-Bench, a benchmark for testing whether self-evolving agents can learn a hidden rule from feedback alone. Each chain adds one rule per level, and each rule applies to an opaque label that stands for a named grouping published on the Web. Six recent self-evolution methods barely learn with a certifying base model, but adding a fixed lesson stating the naming convention raises their scores by 14.5 to 16.5 points. With the stronger GPT-6-Sol, some methods learn from feedback alone.

entry.title: AutoHebb: self-modifying neural networks that infer new tasks without training and keep learning continuously
entry.summary: AutoHebb: Self-Modifying Neural Networks that Zero-Shot Infer and Continually Learn arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces AutoHebb, a class of online feedforward neural networks that learn autonomously. The networks combine external feedback with internal activity to produce a global learning signal that gates a biologically grounded three-factor Hebbian update of plastic weights. Using meta-learning to find fixed weights, the authors report that AutoHebb succeeds on zero-shot inference and continual learning tasks and outperforms modern learning models.

entry.title: DyCraft: An Agentic System for Long-Horizon 4D Scene Generation
entry.summary: DyCraft: An Agentic System for Long-Horizon 4D Scene Generation arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents DyCraft, a system that generates animated 3D scenes by borrowing the workflow of human animators. It breaks the task into steps coding agents can handle more reliably: expanding the prompt into a plan, building a static scene, creating a 3D storyboard of key poses, and authoring motion between verified start and end states. Across 24 long-horizon, multi-shot animation tasks, DyCraft substantially reduces physical violations compared with a native GPT-6 agent and prior agentic baselines, and its outputs are more often preferred by human raters.

entry.title: PathoJev: A pathology model that answers multiple slide questions efficiently from shared visual context.
entry.summary: PathoJev: Efficient Pathology Decisions from Shared Visual Context arXiv · Oct 30, 2026PathoJev is a pathology model that directly predicts answer probabilities for several questions about the same whole slide or region, instead of generating separate text responses. It encodes each slide once and evaluates question suffixes in batches over the shared visual context, reusing recurrent states to limit added computation. Across three whole-slide benchmarks, its 9B and 27B versions reach mean accuracies of 77.2% and 78.1%, exceeding SlideChat by 5.4 and 6.3 points, and the 9B model runs 9.1 times faster than SlideChat on WSI-Bench.

entry.title: Combinatorial Residual Network: a classifier that uses the decay chain to handle jet assignment without explicit labels
entry.summary: Combinatorial Residual Network: a decay-chain-aware classifier without explicit jet assignment arXiv · Oct 30, 2026Particles that decay into several jets require each jet to be matched to its parent particle. The Combinatorial Residual Network (CoReNet) builds its representation along the assumed decay chain, evaluates every jet assignment with shared weights, and combines these hypotheses with learned weights, training on the classification loss alone. On simulated Higgs boson pair production in the bb̄bb̄ final state against QCD multijet background, its 1508 parameters outperform kinematic baselines. It also performs comparably to a transformer network over two orders of magnitude larger on HH→bb̄W⁺W⁻ against semileptonic tt̄.

entry.title: Mage-VL-Cowork: A Full Training Recipe for Hybrid Computer-Use Agents Learned from Evolved Harnesses
entry.summary: Mage-VL-Cowork: A Full Training Recipe to Learn Hybrid Computer Use From Evolved Harnesses arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents Mage-VL-Cowork, a 4B-parameter computer-use agent that combines visual GUI interaction with code and terminal execution in one policy. It is trained through a five-stage curriculum spanning midtraining, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning. The authors also introduce Mage-CUA-Forge, a workflow that synthesizes 293,806 desktop and web tasks across 6,915 skills, and evolve the teacher harness to produce high-quality trajectories. The model reaches 66.0% on OSWorld-Verified, which the authors report as state-of-the-art at its parameter size.

entry.title: Method for certified behavioral retention during continual model adaptation using held-out anchor data
entry.summary: Certified Behavioral Retention for Continual Adaptation with Held-Out Anchors arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper introduces CABA, a post-update gate that keeps historical observations aside from candidate training and compares old and new policies on frozen representations. It accepts the largest tested interpolation coefficient whose worst-anchor forward KL divergence stays within a declared budget. In a UCI Human Activity Recognition study, at budget 0.05, mean forgetting fell from 1.01% to 0.00% while final average accuracy dropped from 93.04% to 88.48%.

entry.title: Apriel Voice 27B Preview: An Open Model for Speech, Reasoning, and Tool Use
entry.summary: Apriel Voice 27B Preview: An Open Model for Speech, Reasoning, and Tool Use arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper presents Apriel Voice 27B Preview, an open speech-language model that combines speech understanding, reasoning, conversation, and tool calling on a shared backbone while keeping text and image inputs. Built on the post-trained Gemma 4 26B-A4B checkpoint, it processes speech directly and produces responses and tool calls without a separate dialogue model. The authors describe a two-stage training procedure and report benchmark results, including 98.90 on Big Bench Audio and a mean latency of 1.91 seconds.

entry.title: Unsupervised feature selection using local intrinsic dimensionality, an extended version
entry.summary: Unsupervised Feature Selection Using Local Intrinsic Dimensionality -- Extended Version arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper proposes LIDFS, an unsupervised feature selection method that ranks features by their local intrinsic dimensionality (LID), estimated from distances to each feature's nearest neighboring features. Lower-LID features receive higher scores, and a refinement step keeps one representative per neighborhood. The method uses no labels and is compared with classic and state-of-the-art methods on 23 high-dimensional datasets. It ranks first in supervised evaluations and first or tied second in clustering evaluations.

entry.title: A model-independent method for finding new physics using smoothed data when the background model is imperfect
entry.summary: Model-Agnostic Search for New Physics in the Presence of Imperfect Background by Smearing the Data arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper presents MASSIB, a method for searching for new particles in high-energy physics without strong assumptions about the signal or background. It uses machine learning to estimate how events compare to an imperfect background model and defines the signal region where this ratio is high. To reduce bias when extrapolating from the control region to the signal region, it introduces a smeared density ratio. Tests on simulated Large Hadron Collider events show high signal concentration and accurate background estimation across different signal types.

entry.title: Beyond Imputation: Task-Aware Diffusion for Edge Anomaly Detection
entry.summary: Don't Just Impute, Detect: Task-Aware Diffusion Pipelines for Edge Anomaly Detection arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper addresses industrial IoT edge pipelines that lose contiguous multi-sensor data, where standard imputers trained only for mean squared error smooth anomalies back toward normal patterns. It proposes the Task-Aware Diffusion Refiner (TADR), a conditional diffusion model trained against a frozen downstream detector's loss, with task-aware terms acting on the one-step clean-window estimate. On SMD, TADR raises F1 by 0.338 over the unrefined detector and runs in 41.4 ms per window on a single CPU core.

entry.title: Bayesian power grid state estimation using flow matching
entry.summary: Bayesian Distribution System State Estimation with Flow Matching arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper addresses distribution system state estimation on medium-voltage feeders, which have few real-time measurements. It proposes PoSE, a method that learns the distribution of substation injections with a neural network trained by flow matching on historical data, while power flow, topology and measurements are incorporated at sampling time through a noise-aware Kalman-type correction. On IEEE 33-bus and 240-bus unbalanced three-phase feeder tests, PoSE gives lower injection, voltage and branch-current errors than Gaussian priors and supervised estimators, with more reliable uncertainty intervals.

entry.title: Li²SAO: A lightweight asynchronous RL method using group-relative actor-critic bootstrapping for LLM training
entry.summary: Li²SAO: Lifting Light Singl-Rollout Asynchronous RL Optimization via Group-Relative Actor-Critic Bootstrapping arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies asynchronous reinforcement learning for post-training large language models, focusing on single-rollout optimization as an alternative to GRPO's group-wise sampling. It finds that its lightweight reproduction, LiSAO, without a pretrained value model trails GRPO on reasoning tasks and lags early in training, though it performs better on agentic tasks. The authors propose Li²SAO, which uses group-relative advantages and group-centered returns while the critic is untrained, then switches to single-rollout GAE. Experiments reportedly show it matches or exceeds GRPO early on and raises the later performance ceiling.

entry.title: INLA-based adaptive UAV sampling for IoT radio maps: prior width sets accuracy and calibration
entry.summary: INLA for Adaptive UAV Sampling of Radio Environment Maps in IoT Networks: Prior Width Governs Accuracy and Calibration arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies adaptive UAV sampling to build radio environment maps from non-Gaussian IoT measurements. It updates a Matérn GMRF posterior with integrated nested Laplace approximation and selects waypoints using entropy pre-screening and Sherman–Morrison lookahead. Posterior-informed sampling yields lower residual NMSE than random and lawnmower sampling, and widening the prior shadowing standard deviation improves NMSE and credible-interval coverage, though overconfidence persists.

entry.title: Sharp rates for estimating shared subspaces in multitask learning
entry.summary: The Geometry of Multitask Learning: Sharp Rates for Shared Subspace Estimation arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies estimation of a shared subspace in multitask learning, noting that existing upper-bound techniques leave exact rates poorly understood. The authors propose a general multitask lemma giving sufficient geometric conditions on task regression functions and their estimators for fast subspace estimation. Applying it, they derive previously unknown sharp minimax rates for linear regression and classification, and rates matching up to logarithmic factors for additive-noise regression.

entry.title: Automatically Building Strong Simple Baselines
entry.summary: Automatic Construction of Strong Simple Baselines arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper examines whether large language models can automatically construct simple baselines to test whether deep learning methods in science genuinely add value. The authors assemble 36 supervised classification and regression tasks from peer-reviewed studies in Nature, Science, and Cell-family journals. The automatically built baselines recover a median of 95.5% (mean 85.7%) of the gap between a trivial predictor and the deep learning score, and matching or exceeding the deep learning model in 12 studies.

entry.title: CalibCause: A Quality-Gated, Interpretable and Calibrated Deep Learning Framework for Diabetic Retinopathy Grading
entry.summary: CalibCause: A Quality-Gated, Interpretable and Calibrated Deep Learning Framework for Diabetic Retinopathy Grading arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper presents CalibCause, a deep learning framework for grading diabetic retinopathy that combines image-quality conditioning, per-expert visual explanations, knowledge distillation, and calibrated confidence with deferral. The framework was evaluated on 51,310 fundus images from EyePACS, DDR, and APTOS 2019, with IDRiD and DeepDRiD used for external testing. The authors report that the distilled student model performs comparably to a plain baseline across sites while using fewer parameters. They conclude that reliable deployment still requires local validation and adaptation.

entry.title: CausalGrade: Scoring Candidate Causal Graphs Using Evidence-Guided Judgments
entry.summary: CausalGrade: Evidence-Guided Causal Graph Scoring with Jev arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces CausalGrade, a method for scoring candidate causal graphs when the true causal structure is unknown. It uses the probabilistic judgment model Jev, combining association, conditional dependence, and directionality evidence from observational data with edge probabilities from the CDFM foundation model. A graph-level score is derived by measuring agreement between the graph's adjacency structure and Jev's edge-level judgments. On synthetic data, the score negatively correlates with structural error, and it achieves a 54.4% best-candidate hit rate in graph selection tasks, above the 48.4% of the Self-Compatibility metric.

entry.title: AI agents that tune cosmology simulations using large language models
entry.summary: Agentic Systems for Calibrating Cosmological Simulations arXiv · Oct 27, 2026Calibrating cosmological simulations requires costly optimization over many parameters.
