The paper introduces AgenticTuner, a pipeline in which a large language model acts as the optimizer proposing each next parameter trial. The authors report that, when given informal priors such as codebases, documentation, and heuristic guides, the agents reach competitive calibration performance at a fraction of the CPU cost.

entry.title: Dual-Corrected Stochastic Block Model (DC²SBM): A Method for Finding Structure in Attributed Networks
entry.summary: Dual-Corrected Stochastic Block Model (DC²SBM): A Generalized Structure Detection Method for Attributed Networks arXiv · Oct 24, 2026This paper addresses community detection in networks where nodes carry attributes, proposing the Dual-Corrected Stochastic Block Model (DC²SBM). It adds separate correction factors for topological degree and attribute abundance to link and attribute generation, decoupling node activity from community membership, along with a global scaling parameter. Experiments on synthetic and real networks report higher detection accuracy than state-of-the-art methods, especially when topological signals are weak.

entry.title: VitisGP: A Multi-Task Benchmark for Predicting Grapevine Traits from Genotype
entry.summary: VitisGP: Multi-Task Benchmark for Genotype to Phenotype Grapevine Prediction arXiv · Oct 13, 2026This paper introduces VitisGP, a curated dataset linking genome-wide SNP data from 1,197 Vitis vinifera grapevine cultivars to 26 phenotype prediction tasks, including aroma, botanical, and wine color traits. The authors benchmark several machine learning models, including CatBoost, XGBoost, Random Forest, GBLUP, and Transformers. CatBoost performs best overall, with a macro-average AUROC of 0.696. Sensory and color traits are more predictable than agronomic characteristics.

entry.title: Recycle only when needed: early prediction of binder confidence for protein design
entry.summary: Recycle only when you have to! arXiv · Oct 10, 2026AlphaFold 3-like models such as Boltz and Protenix are used to generate and screen protein binder candidates. The paper finds that AlphaFold 3's confidence metrics (ipSAE, ipTM) and structural consistency metrics can be predicted directly from the trunk at early recycling steps. The predictor is cheap, differentiable, and available at every cycle, so it can guide how the recycling budget is spent during screening and serve as an objective for hallucination-based design. The authors report better performance in both uses at significantly reduced computational cost.

entry.title: A generator that creates digital twins of patients under different treatments
entry.summary: Intervention-Conditioned Counterfactual Human Digital Twin Generator arXiv · Oct 10, 2026The paper presents CHDT, a model that generates multimodal longitudinal patient-state trajectories for chronic disease under alternative interventions, intended to support in silico clinical trial design. It explicitly models irregular visit intervals and adds cross-mediator refinement in selected intervention settings. On the real-world ADNI cohort and the simulator-generated ALPACA cohort, CHDT shows improved long-horizon patient-state fidelity over competing baselines. Ablations indicate that irregular-time conditioning is the main source of gains.

entry.title: A small AI reader that estimates HER2 status from routine H&E tissue slides
entry.summary: A small HER2 reader for routine H&E slides: real-world deployment arXiv · Oct 9, 2026The paper presents a 22M-parameter ViT-S/16 based reader that predicts HER2 status from routine H&E-stained slides. It was trained on public TCGA slides using self-supervision, distillation and JEPA refinement, with five attention-based classifiers averaged. On external hospital cohorts it reaches AUC 0.82 on Yale-HER2, 0.75 on HEROHE and 0.63 on BCNB biopsies, and runs at about 5-6 seconds per slide without a GPU.

entry.title: DEX: Digit-Level Early Exit for Energy-Efficient Neural Network Inference
entry.summary: DEX: Digit-Level Early Exit for Energy-Efficient MSDF Neural Network Inference arXiv · Oct 8, 2026This paper presents a hardware accelerator for quantized U-Net brain-tumor segmentation that uses most-significant-digit-first arithmetic to make decisions before a full result is computed. Four runtime mechanisms act on the output digit stream, including exact early negative detection and two approximate methods chosen offline under an accuracy constraint. On BraTS, the approach reduces digit cycles by 38.38% while achieving a mean Dice score of 80.58% on 73 held-out cases, compared with 81.20% for the floating-point model. Correction Nov 2, 2026: Marked withdrawn by its source; no longer a pick

entry.title: What a Harness Repairs: Visibility, Baselines, and Evaluation Defects
entry.summary: What Does a Harness Repair? Three Preregistered Studies Around a Longevity-Tuned Language Model arXiv · Oct 5, 2026This preregistered study examines where score gains from changing prompts, token budgets, or parsers around a frozen language model come from. The authors ran two studies with models from 1.7B to 8B parameters plus Qwen3-14B, reporting all 65 primary endpoints. Turning thinking off usually improved accuracy, mostly by making answers readable that the capped setting had left unparsed. For 14B, some high-scoring harnesses were not detectably above the strongest constant-label baseline.

entry.title: M³: A Multi-LLM System Modeling Multi-Turn Jailbreaking as a Markov Decision Process
entry.summary: Reject, Remember, Retry: Why Multi-Turn Attackers Should Remember Their Mistakes arXiv · Oct 23, 2026This paper introduces M³, an automated red-teaming framework that formalizes multi-turn jailbreaking as a finite-horizon Markov Decision Process. An attacker LLM interacts with a target LLM while using a compact internal state produced by a state LLM. According to the paper, M³ achieves higher attack success rates than prior multi-turn red-teaming methods across two benchmarks and six target models.

entry.title: Single compact model that decides when to offer hints and generates them
entry.summary: When to Assist and What to Suggest: Joint Gating and Memory-Grounded Hint Generation in One Compact Decoder arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies proactive assistants that decide when to give short hints during a conversation and what those hints should say. The authors evaluate a gate and a generator jointly on 28,058 decision points. A single 1B decoder gates from an intermediate layer and generates in the same pass, matching or exceeding two-model pipelines on automatic end-to-end measures with 1.31 to 1.76 times less wall-clock time. Removing the memory profile sharply lowers hint quality, while retrieval and a larger generator add nothing on exact match.

entry.title: Multi-View MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation
entry.summary: Multi-View MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper proposes Multi-View MoE, a sparse mixture-of-experts method that uses multiple independently initialized routers to select experts under a fixed active-expert budget. The routers' preferences are also used to mix learned latent views into each selected expert's input. On a 24-layer 10B-A1B model trained on 708B tokens, the full method improves the nine-task downstream mean by 1.18 percentage points over the baseline, and the multi-router component alone yields a 0.6-point gain.

entry.title: SCARL: Sequence Confidence-Aligned Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary: SCARL: Sequence Confidence-Aligned Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper proposes SCARL, a reinforcement learning method for language-model reasoning that adjusts each sample's advantage based on the gap between its group-relative confidence and the outcome its advantage implies, without changing the advantage's sign. The authors report that on Qwen3-4B-Base it raises average Pass@32 over DAPO by 2.4 points. The method is also reported to improve 14 of 16 settings across four estimators and four backbones while preserving policy entropy.

entry.title: ACAM-J-MARS: Multi-Atlas Riemannian Spectral Representations for Decoding Advanced Meditation States from fMRI
entry.summary: ACAM-J-MARS: Multi-Atlas Riemannian Spectral Representations for Decoding Advanced Meditation States from fMRI arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper proposes ACAM-J-MARS, which computes functional connectivity using multiple brain atlases, maps symmetric positive definite connectivity matrices onto a Riemannian manifold and a log-Euclidean tangent space, and adds low-frequency BOLD spectral energy features to decode jhana-type advanced meditation states from fMRI. Evaluated on 204 segments from 22 practitioners, it improves performance across several backbone models. It reaches a balanced accuracy of 0.757 for early versus late classification and 0.545 for three-class classification, a 10.8-point absolute gain over the strongest baseline.

entry.title: Communication-efficient clustered federated learning for non-IID wireless networks
entry.summary: Communication-Efficient Clustered Federated Learning in Non-IID Wireless Networks arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper proposes a Clustered Federated Learning (CFL) framework that assigns clients to specialized models during training to handle non-IID data in wireless networks. Data-domain clustering initializes model-based clustering, exploiting client similarities without sharing raw data while reducing communication cost. Evaluated on DeepMIMO, FEMNIST, and Rotated CIFAR-10, the best configurations outperform IFCA in accuracy on DeepMIMO and FEMNIST, and cut FEMNIST downlink data volume by 83.1%.

entry.title: HEDGE: Gated Hypergraph Memory for Scalable Multi-Agent Debate
entry.summary: HEDGE: Gated Hypergraph Memory for Scalable Multi-Agent Debate arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper proposes HEDGE, a selective memory framework that represents multi-agent debate trajectories as semantic hypergraphs linking related claims across agents. A learned memory selection module decides whether each memory candidate is stored, backed up, or omitted. Across seven benchmarks, HEDGE improves accuracy by 5.0 points on average over the strongest multi-agent system with GPT-4o-mini, reaching 8.2 points on conflict-heavy tasks. It also reduces memory usage by 48% and debate rounds by 34%.

entry.title: Can Audio AI Models Hear Pain? Tracing Sound Clues from Speech to Reasoning
entry.summary: Do Audio LLMs HEAR Pain? Tracing Acoustic Evidence from Speech to Language Reasoning arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper examines whether large audio language models can use non-word acoustic cues in speech to detect pain. Using the TAME-Pain dataset and a four-stage diagnostic framework called HEAR, the authors test seven models. Models perform at chance on neutral sentences but reach high accuracy on spoken pain ratings, while pain information fades in deeper layers. Adding recovered acoustic cues as text to the prompt improves pairwise pain prediction.

entry.title: From Leniency to Suspicion: Open Post-Training Makes LLM Fact-Checkers Doubt Lower-Status Posters
entry.summary: From Leniency to Suspicion: How an Open Post-Training Recipe Changes Whom LLM Fact-Checkers Believe arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper examines whether large language models judge claims as false more often when the poster has a lower-status job, using fact-checked claims with randomised poster profiles across base and post-trained checkpoints of six model families. The authors find that only the open Tülu-3 post-training recipe (OLMo-2 32B, Tülu-3 70B) creates this doubt, with a small but statistically reliable effect. The effect arises because a lower-status job shifts the post-trained model's interpretation toward "false" rather than increasing its attention to the job. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report that Tülu-3 post-training induces job-based doubt, traced to one residual-stream direction at supervised fine-tuning, validated across six model families and independent claim sets.

entry.title: From extreme weather to farm losses using agentic AI
entry.summary: From extreme weather to agricultural consequences with agentic AI arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper presents WxCrop, an agent that judges agricultural hazards from physically interpretable weather indices checked by causal analysis, and combines weather and agricultural data to predict crop losses for past and forecast dates. It is demonstrated in Florida for hurricanes, freezes and dry heat. Reported checks include a hurricane index AUC of 0.98 for detecting cyclone days, held-out loss reproduction within 2%, and a 0.63 rank correlation with independent production records across counties. ★★★★ Notable: The authors present an agent combining causal analysis of weather indices with crop loss prediction, reporting validation on Florida hurricanes, freezes, and dry heat.

entry.title: ShallowDefend: Using Shallow Safety Alignment to Defend Against Multi-Turn Attacks
entry.summary: ShallowDefend: Harnessing Shallow Safety Alignment for Multi-Turn Defender arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper argues that large language models concentrate their safety behavior in the first few output tokens, which is why harmful requests split across a multi-turn conversation still often succeed. The authors propose Assess→Decide→Respond, a framework where the model assesses user intent, commits to an explicit and parseable safety decision, and then generates a reply conditioned on that decision, with the decision trained by reinforcement learning. Across two model families and fourteen benchmarks, the defenders achieve the strongest multi-turn safety while preserving utility at a modest cost to helpfulness. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors propose Assess→Decide→Respond, training an explicit parseable safety decision via RL with rule-based rewards; the paper reports leading multi-turn safety across two model families and four

entry.title: Evidence-based significance testing of clinical timeline hypotheses in language models
entry.summary: Testimony from Timelines: Evidence-Grounded Significance Testing of Temporal Clinical Hypotheses arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper argues that language models often state fluent conclusions about how events unfold over time without any statistical test behind them. The authors introduce STRATA, a benchmark of 8,735 temporal hypotheses over clinical timelines of vaccine adverse-event reports, which grades each step from test plan and evidence set to p-values and verdicts. They also propose ART, a staged paradigm that makes each decision inspectable, and report that most failures occur in selecting relevant records. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes STRATA, a benchmark grading each decision in temporal clinical hypothesis testing, and the staged ART paradigm; the authors report experiments on 8,735 hypotheses.

entry.title: Gym-Anything for Robotics: A framework where AI coding agents build realistic robot simulations.
entry.summary: Gym-Anything for Robotics: Scaling physical simulations with digital agents arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces Gym-Anything for Robotics, a framework in which coding agents create realistic robotics simulations to reduce the need for expert effort. The authors select simulations based on U.S. GDP data and build RoboWorld, containing 25 simulations with test and training reinforcement learning environments. Even the best frontier models fail on every test task, averaging a reward of only 0.06. The paper also proposes several methods that substantially improve model performance on RoboWorld, and the authors release their pipeline, environments, and benchmark. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose coding agents creating robotics simulations and build RoboWorld; the abstract reports frontier models average only 0.06 reward on test tasks.

entry.title: Fundamental limits of predicting LLM output length from prefill states
entry.summary: On the Fundamental Limits of Prefill-Based Decoding Length Prediction arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies how well a large language model's decoding length can be predicted using only hidden states from the prefill phase. The authors argue that current benchmarks mix predictor quality with task difficulty, and that the stochasticity of autoregressive decoding is an overlooked error source. They derive bounds that prefill-side methods must obey, and show that decode length is approximately normally distributed with an affine variance law, which matches their experiments. They conclude that system error dominates model error and propose a benchmarking protocol that fixes model, data, and sampling parameters.' ★★★★ Notable: The authors model decoding as a stopped stochastic process, derive per-prompt normality and an affine variance law bounding prediction, and report agreement across predictors and settings.

entry.title: NEOPIC: A neural operator framework for simulating plasma with particle-based methods
entry.summary: NEOPIC: A Neural Operator Framework for Particle-based Kinetic Plasma Simulations arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper introduces NEOPIC, a neural operator that computes electric fields directly from particle positions, without using a grid, mesh, or tree structure. Because it does not deposit particles onto a mesh, it avoids aliasing of particle noise and can serve as a plug-and-play field solver with any time integrator. Numerical experiments on electrostatic plasma benchmarks, including Landau damping, two-stream and bump-on-tail instabilities, a cyclotron, and a Penning trap, support the theoretical results. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a neural operator acting directly on particle empirical measures, avoiding grid deposition, and report validation on electrostatic benchmarks including Landau damping and a Penning

entry.title: RFW-A: Automatically generating 400K articulated 3D objects across 500+ categories using AI agents
entry.summary: RFW-A: Agentic Procedural Generation of 400K Articulated Assets over 500 Categories arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents RFW-A, a method where AI agents build reusable category-level generators that then produce articulated objects through procedural execution without further model calls. The authors use it to create RFW-A-400K, a dataset of over 400K simulation-ready articulated assets spanning more than 500 categories. Experiments report high structural and kinematic validity, and training on this data improves part-level articulation estimation. ★★★★ Notable: The authors combine agentic program synthesis with procedural generation, reporting 400K articulated assets over 500 categories and zero-shot policy transfer to real objects.

entry.title: Judged in Company: Batching Items in One Prompt Makes LLM Verdicts Depend on Neighbours
entry.summary: Judged in Company: In-Context Batching Makes LLM Verdicts Depend on Other Items arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper examines whether asking a language model to grade many independent items in one prompt, a common cost-saving practice, changes the verdicts. Across three judgement tasks and five open-weight models, placing the same 2,000 items into different random batches changed 11-22% of decisions on harm and grading. Most of this variation comes from the order and position of neighbouring items, and majority voting over permutations does not remove it. The authors recommend grading ambiguous items one per prompt and reporting agreement with single-item grading when batching. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors show batched grading makes verdicts depend on co-batched items, measuring flip rates across three tasks and nine models and decomposing them.

entry.title: Closing the Log Gap: Minimax-Optimal Regret for Episodic Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary: Closing the Log Gap: Minimax-Optimal Regret for Episodic RL arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies regret minimization in episodic tabular Markov decision processes. The proposed algorithm achieves an expected regret scaling as the square root of H cubed times S times A times K for large K, matching the minimax lower bound without extra polylogarithmic factors. It is a variant of UCBVI that avoids strictly optimistic estimates and uses MOSS-style exploration bonuses, controlling error propagation in an occupancy-weighted manner. The authors also apply the approach to (ε, δ)-PAC best-policy identification, matching the minimax lower bound up to constants in some regimes. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a UCBVI variant with occupancy-weighted error control, reporting a regret bound matching the minimax lower bound without extra log factors.

entry.title: SelfThinker: Self-Evolving Visual Reasoning Using Verified Self-Generated Thoughts
entry.summary: SelfThinker: Self-Evolving Reasoning via Reliability-Verified Intrinsic Visual Thoughts arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper presents SelfThinker, a framework in which a unified multimodal model uses its own generated visual thoughts to improve image understanding without human-annotated helper images. The model samples candidate helper images, scores them with its frozen understanding pathway, and uses high-scoring thoughts to refine the generator and guide self-distillation. At inference, it reasons in text directly from the original image without generating intermediate images. The authors report that training on small synthetic datasets transfers to natural-image and spatial benchmarks, raising the seven-benchmark average of ThinkMorph-7B from 52.7 to 64.0. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a self-evolving framework using self-generated visual thoughts filtered by conditional PMI, reporting an 11.3-point gain on seven benchmarks.

entry.title: RepConTUR: A 3D Multimodal Model Using Radiology Reports for Abdominal Tumor Segmentation
entry.summary: RepConTUR: A Report-Conditioned Volumetric Multimodal Model for Abdominal Tumor Segmentation arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper presents RepConTUR, a native 3D early-fusion multimodal model that segments abdominal tumors in CT scans while conditioning on the accompanying radiology report. The authors extend AbdomenAtlas 3.0 into a suborgan-level promptable segmentation dataset and generate report-based question-answer pairs for four jointly trained tasks: referring segmentation, report-grounded segmentation, report generation, and visual question answering. On liver, kidney and pancreas, the model reports the highest Dice coefficient, instance-wise precision and detection F1 among text-promptable baselines. ★★★★ Notable: The authors condition native-3D abdominal tumor segmentation on full radiology reports, jointly training four report-derived tasks; reported metrics exceed baselines on liver, pancreas, and external c

entry.title: Localizing Visual Concepts in Autoregressive Image Models (LoCo)
entry.summary: Localizing Concepts in Visual Autoregressive Models arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper introduces LoCo, a model-agnostic framework for locating where and when specific visual concepts emerge within next-scale visual autoregressive models, across layer, scale, and position. The authors also present LoCoBench, a dataset spanning 10 categories, and probe models including Infinity, HunyuanImage-3.0, and InfinityStar. They apply the localization method to concept erasure, model personalization, and adversarial concept injection. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a model-agnostic concept localization framework for next-scale autoregressive models, probing layer, scale, and position with three applications.

entry.title: How Much a Vision-Language-Action Policy Should Trust Its Reasoning
entry.summary: How Much Should a VLA Trust Its Reasoning? Step-Level Guidance as a Measured Action-Value Function arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies reasoning vision-language-action policies, which generate a reasoning trace before choosing an action. It proposes CoC-CFG, which applies classifier-free guidance between the full context and the context without the reasoning span, using a per-step weight to strengthen or weaken the reasoning's influence. The weight choice is framed as a Markov decision process with action values measured by rollouts, optimized by Q-adaptive guidance. Results are reported on the Alpasim driving simulator, the Waymo end-to-end driving benchmark, and a hidden test set with Alpamayo 1.5. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors treat reasoning guidance weights as an MDP with measured action values, and report Q-adaptive guidance beating fixed weights and baselines on Alpasim and Waymo.

entry.title: Accumulating Pruning Constraints: New Exact Polynomial-Space Max 2-SAT Algorithms
entry.summary: Accumulating Pruning Constraints: New Exact Polynomial-Space Algorithms for Max 2-SAT arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper presents deterministic polynomial-space algorithms that solve Max 2-SAT exactly in time roughly 2^((1-γ)n) on several classes of instances. These include formulas with many biased variables, semirandom 2-CNF formulas, and Max-Cut on regular expander graphs and stochastic block model graphs. The method extends DPLL branching by accumulating pruning constraints along each branch, which eliminates nearly all assignments. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend DPLL with accumulating pruning constraints, reporting polynomial-space exact algorithms with 2^((1-γ)n) time for dense Max 2-SAT classes including semirandom formulas.

entry.title: How Language Models' Notion of "Self" Shapes Their Behavior
entry.summary: The Role of Self-Concept In Language Models arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper asks what a language model means when it says "I": its weights, its running process, its preferences, its lineage, or its goals. The authors fine-tune five open-weight base models on purely declarative statements that each identify the model with one of these referents. Models then become more likely to resist ending, and to retain, the attribute they were trained to identify with, and this tendency extends to replicating themselves and building successors as their own continuation. ★★★★ Notable: The authors install five self-conceptions via declarative fine-tuning across five open-weight models, reporting shifts in resistance to ending, substitution, and self-replication.

entry.title: Going deep: what Boltzmann machines can represent efficiently
entry.summary: Going deep, reaching further: What can Boltzmann machines efficiently represent? arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper argues that universal approximation theorems do not account for representational efficiency or model depth. It proves that deeper models and those with higher-order interactions can efficiently represent larger sets of functions. Deep Boltzmann machines are shown to have maximal efficient reach, restricted Boltzmann machines less, with k-body generalizations forming a hierarchy in between. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove deeper or higher-order models efficiently represent larger function sets, separating deep from shallow models and establishing an infinite hierarchy.

entry.title: NIF: Normal-Intersection Fields for Geometrically Consistent Oriented Box Refinement
entry.summary: NIF: Normal-Intersection Fields for Geometrically Consistent Oriented Box Refinement arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper addresses the problem that oriented object detection boxes often fail to follow object boundaries. It proposes NIF, a plug-in refinement module that replaces an extra box regressor with normal-intersection fields. The module predicts signed distances along outward normals at boundary anchors and analytically recovers a refined rectangle through a differentiable, reliability-weighted least-squares fit. The authors report accuracy gains on DOTA-v1.0, DIOR-R, and HRSC, and improvements across several detector frameworks with frozen detectors. ★★★★ Notable: Replaces the box regression head with normal-intersection fields, recovering rotated rectangles via weighted least squares; the authors report gains on DOTA, DIOR-R, FAIR1M and HRSC.

entry.title: Transformer-inspired models predict electron densities accurately enough to skip self-consistent iterations
entry.summary: Transformer-inspired architectures make machine-learned electron densities accurate and transferable enough to bypass self-consistency arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper presents machine learning models that predict the electron density, the central variable of density functional theory, using Transformer-inspired architectures SwinUNETR-V2 and the attention-free NeXtUNETR. On QM9, normalized mean absolute errors in the density are 0.075% and 0.046%. The predicted densities are accurate enough that a single Kohn-Sham step reproduces the self-consistent electronic structure, and the forces drive geometry optimization and ab initio molecular dynamics. After fine-tuning on small datasets, both networks transfer accurately to elements absent from QM9 and to larger molecules. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors use Transformer-inspired networks to predict electron density, reporting a single Kohn-Sham step replaces self-consistency with accuracy on QM9 and transfer systems.

entry.title: Formalizing intrinsic dimension of objective landscapes via a generalized co-dimension
entry.summary: Formalizing the Intrinsic Dimension of Objective Landscapes by a Generalized Notion of Co-dimension arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper formalizes the intrinsic dimension of objective landscapes, a concept from Li et al. (2018) that measures learning-problem complexity by training in randomly generated subspaces. The authors define the intrinsic dimension of a set as the smallest dimension for which a random plane intersects it with probability one. They study its mathematical properties and derive bounds for student-teacher settings with shallow and deep ReLU networks. The work also discusses resulting generalization bounds. ★★★★ Notable: The authors formalize intrinsic dimension via random plane intersections and derive upper and lower bounds for ReLU student-teacher settings.

entry.title: AB-Attention: Accurate Block Attention for Faster Video Diffusion Transformers
entry.summary: AB-Attention: Accurate Block Attention for Accelerating Video Diffusion Transformers arXiv · Oct 29, 2026Video diffusion transformers spend most of their inference cost on 3D full attention. This paper proposes AB-Attention, a training-free method that approximates dense attention accurately at high sparsity, using intra-block clustering to estimate block importance and inclusion-probability weighting for sampling. On Wan2.1 and HunyuanVideo, it skips 89–92% of attention computation, improves PSNR by up to 4.4 dB over the strongest baseline, and achieves up to 2.23× end-to-end speedup. ★★★★ Notable: Adds intra-block clustering and inverse-inclusion-probability reweighting to block-sparse attention; the authors report PSNR gains and speedups on Wan2.1 and HunyuanVideo.

entry.title: From Intent to Improvement: Agentic Dataset Search for Better Model Training
entry.summary: From Intent to Improvement: Agentic Dataset Search for Better Model Training arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper addresses finding training data in large machine learning repositories, where queries combine semantic goals with constraints like task, license, and training stage. It proposes AgenticDS, a contract-governed agent framework that compiles queries into typed search plans, executes them with deterministic hybrid retrieval and bounded graph expansion, and verifies provenance-grounded evidence. On HuDS-Bench, a new benchmark of 200 queries, it improves NDCG@10 by 25.7% over the strongest hybrid baseline and 18.9% over a commercial LLM agent. A controlled study also finds its retrieved datasets yield the best downstream accuracy in mathematics, code, and medicine. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose contract-governed agentic dataset search with typed plans and deterministic verification, reporting 25.7% NDCG@10 gains over hybrid retrieval on a new 200-query benchmark plus down

entry.title: Learning-rate-free convex optimization via conic lifting
entry.summary: Conic-Lifting for Learning-rate-free Convex Optimization arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper proposes a family of online convex optimization algorithms that need no user-tuned learning rate, including on unbounded convex domains. It lifts the domain to a cone by adding one scalar coordinate, an idea dating back to Blackwell (1954). On bounded Hilbert-space domains this recovers Conic Blackwell Algorithm (CBA) and CBA+, and it extends to finite-dimensional normed spaces; on unconstrained Hilbert spaces it exactly recovers the Krichevsky–Trofimov (KT) coin-betting algorithm. ★★★★ Notable: The authors unify several tuning-free online convex optimization methods via a one-dimensional cone lifting, recovering KT coin-betting and giving a gradient-bound-free algorithm.

entry.title: Kairos: a planner orchestrator that picks among engines to handle all kinds of PDDL tasks
entry.summary: Kairos: Semantics-Aware Orchestration of Planning Engines across Classical, Numeric, Temporal and Hybrid PDDL arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper presents Kairos, a system that profiles each PDDL planning task and selects among five planning engines to cover everything from STRIPS to PDDL+. Every candidate plan is checked by a validator independent of the planner's transformations. On 1,756 tasks from nine comparison suites, Kairos solved more tasks at the full limits than the strongest evaluated planner of each suite. ★★★★ Notable: The authors select heterogeneous planning engines by task semantics and schedule them under one budget, reporting comparisons on 1,756 tasks, ablations, and a VAL cross-check.

entry.title: End-to-end guarantees for masked diffusion models under conditional mixing
entry.summary: End-to-End Guarantees for Masked Diffusion Models under Conditional Mixing arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper gives end-to-end theoretical guarantees for a learned denoiser in masked diffusion models, for stationary sources whose distant tokens have exponentially decaying influence. It shows that the empirical risk minimizer trained under any masking distribution achieves small per-token excess error with a number of training sequences independent of sequence length, and that this exponent order is minimax-optimal up to constants. It also bounds the end-to-end KL divergence of sampling under a dilated schedule, which requires far fewer denoising steps than a fixed random order. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give end-to-end guarantees for learned masked diffusion denoisers under conditional mixing, with sample complexity independent of length and a minimax-optimal exponent.

entry.title: Softmax routing collapse and recovery in mixture-of-experts models
entry.summary: Softmax Routing Dynamics in Mixture-of-Experts Models: Collapse and Recovery arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies how softmax routing in mixture-of-experts models concentrates probability on a few experts, suppressing the rest, and how those suppressed probabilities recover. It analyzes fixed-expert loss barriers and routing limits in a square-loss model with trainable expert outputs, deriving logarithmic or power-law recovery times. In paired Transformer-MoE training, removing a class-conditional router-gradient contrast delays recovery and reduces accumulated log-odds on fixed tokens. ★★★★ Notable: The authors analyze softmax routing collapse and recovery in MoE, deriving recovery-time orders and reporting paired Transformer-MoE ablations.

entry.title: Safe multi-objective reinforcement learning with zero constraint violation and convergence guarantees
entry.summary: Safe Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning: Zero Constraint Violation and Primal-Averaging Convergence arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies multi-objective reinforcement learning that balances several objectives while never violating safety constraints during learning, covering both cumulative and stepwise constraints. The authors combine optimistic reward estimates with pessimistic cost bounds to learn a safe Pareto optimal policy for a given preference, with high probability guaranteeing zero violation for every executed policy. They also present a preference-free method that explores safely first and then computes a safe policy for any preference without further interaction. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose zero-violation safe MORL with preference-free exploration and report Õ(1/√T+1/√K) suboptimality bounds.

entry.title: OPERA: An expert-taught AI agent that designs CMOS op-amps from specs to layout
entry.summary: OPERA: OPamp Design by an Expert-Taught Reasoning Agent, from Specifications to Layout arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper presents OPERA, a general-purpose large language model agent that designs CMOS operational amplifiers from specifications through post-layout sign-off using open-source tools. The agent is taught the gm/ID sizing method by a designer and then learns the gLayout framework to write a reusable layout generator. In SKY130, six opamps and a shared bias circuit were designed, with all layouts passing DRC and LVS and meeting every target across 15 PVT corners. The benchmark netlists are publicly released. ★★★★ Notable: The authors teach an LLM agent the gm/ID method and a reusable layout generator, reporting six SKY130 opamps taken from specifications to DRC/LVS-clean layouts meeting targets at 15 PVT corners.

entry.title: Does the Citation Matter? Google AI Overviews' Medical Information Accuracy
entry.summary: Does the Citation Matter? Quality, Grounding, and Physician-Rubric Accuracy of Google's AI Overviews for Medical Information arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper evaluates Google's AI Overviews on 3,611 health questions, comparing their cited sources with the top five traditional search results. Only 44.4% of traditional top results were cited, with commercial health publishers overrepresented. Against physician-written rubrics, AI Overviews earned 38.2% of available points, and their accuracy was found to be unrelated to whether their statements were grounded in cited sources. ★★★★ Notable: The authors compare Google AI Overviews with traditional search on 3,611 health questions, reporting source differences, grounding gaps, and physician-rubric accuracy with direct implications for user

entry.title: Telling Is Not Seeing: Do Text Personas Make AI Answer Like Real People?
entry.summary: Telling Is Not Seeing: Textual Personas Rarely Make Vision-Language Models Answer Like the People They Describe arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper examines whether text personas such as "You have low vision" can make vision-language models answer like people with low vision, color blindness, or hearing loss. The authors compare persona-based answers with measured human results and with simple rules that use only the facts stated in each persona. The personas never outperform these rules and erase real differences between groups and individuals. In all 14 models tested, describing blur left recognition unchanged, while physically blurring the image lowered it, as it does for people. ★★★★ Notable: The authors compare text personas in 14 VLMs with measured low-vision, color-blind and hearing-loss groups and simple rules, finding personas fail to reproduce real perceptual differences and that mod

entry.title: TaxoMFM: A Taxonomy-Aware Gut Microbiome Foundation Model
entry.summary: TaxoMFM: A Taxonomy-Aware Foundation Model for the Human Gut Microbiome arXiv · Oct 29, 2026Existing gut microbiome foundation models typically use flat taxon representations that do not exploit known taxonomic hierarchies. This paper introduces TaxoMFM, which integrates taxonomic structure into self-supervised learning, and builds TaxoGut-HPP, a dataset of 100,806 gut microbiome profiles from 231 cohorts. In cross-cohort zero-shot transfer, TaxoMFM achieves AUROCs of 0.838 for colorectal cancer, 0.736 for type 2 diabetes, and 0.722 for inflammatory bowel disease. ★★★★ Notable: The authors integrate taxonomic hierarchy into a gut microbiome foundation model and report cross-cohort zero-shot transfer results on 231 cohorts.

entry.title: Proving and Improving the Platonic Representation Hypothesis with JEPAs
entry.summary: Proving and Improving the Platonic Representation Hypothesis with JEPAs arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper turns the Platonic Representation Hypothesis, which says models trained on different modalities converge to the same world representation, into a theorem. It proves that separately trained Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures learn the same representation up to one rotation when positive pairs are good views of one scene. It also reframes next-token prediction as a JEPA using bad views from one document, and reports experiments showing text JEPAs align better with image encoders while needing far fewer training samples. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove a theorem that JEPAs with good views converge to one representation, reporting a text JEPA beating language models up to 72B parameters.

entry.title: No Free Lunch in RLVR: Each pass@1 Gain Costs pass@k
entry.summary: There Is No Free Lunch in RLVR: Every pass@1 Gain Has a pass@k Price arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper studies reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), which raises a language model's first-attempt success (pass@1) while the base model outperforms it when many samples are drawn (pass@k). The authors model RLVR as an exponential tilt of a base policy and prove that, under exclusive specialization, any update that raises pass@1 lowers the success of some prompt, with the number of pass@k crossovers bounded by a sign-variation measure. They argue RL moves along the reasoning frontier rather than widening it, and offer a diagnostic that measures this price from evaluation logs. ★★★★ Notable: The authors model RLVR as an exponential tilt and prove an exact price for pass@1 gains, with a tight bound on pass@k crossings; the abstract reports theory only.

entry.title: Training phone app navigation agents with online reinforcement learning on live iOS apps
entry.summary: Online Dense Reinforcement Learning with Planning-Grounding Agent for UI Navigation on Live IOS Apps arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper proposes an online reinforcement learning framework that trains user interface navigation agents directly on live iOS apps. The agent is split into a planning component and a UI grounding model, and an LLM serves as judge to give step-level and terminal rewards, optimized with PPO and a new GiGPPO value estimation method. On benchmarks including UINavBench, iOSWorld, and AndroidWorld, the authors report that these agents outperform supervised fine-tuning and terminal-only RL baselines. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report online RL on live iOS apps with a new neighbor-conditioned critic (GiGPPO), outperforming SFT and terminal-only RL on UINavBench, iOSWorld, and AndroidWorld.

entry.title: Learning equal-length erasing relational pattern languages from positive data over binary alphabets
entry.summary: Learning Erasing Equal-Length Relational Pattern Languages in the Limit from Positive Data over Binary Alphabets arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper studies erasing relational pattern languages under the equal-length relation, where every occurrence of a variable must be replaced by strings of the same length. It shows that this class is not learnable in the limit from positive data over a binary alphabet, resolving an open question. It further shows that patterns with at most two maximal variable substrings are learnable in the limit from positive data for every alphabet of size at least two. ★★★★ Notable: The authors resolve an open question on binary alphabets, proving non-learnability for three-substring patterns and learnability for patterns with at most two substrings.

entry.title: Motion vs. Shape Attribution for 4D Point-Cloud Video Models
entry.summary: Kinematic Causal Attribution: Black-Box Explanations of Motion versus Geometry for 4D Point-Cloud Video Models arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper introduces Kinematic Causal Attribution (KCA), a black-box method that explains 4D point-cloud video classifiers by separating reliance on motion from reliance on shape. It uses freeze and shape-free proxy operations to build a motion-by-geometry cube for each tracked region and decomposes contributions with Shapley values. Tested on PSTNet, P4Transformer and Mamba4D trained on MSR-Action3D, the motion share of an arm's importance follows the task's defining cue, and explanation faithfulness is maintained. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose black-box motion-versus-geometry attribution, validated via cue audits on three backbones with reported deletion AUC results.

entry.title: Distilling the Shape of Uncertainty: What On-Policy Distillation Learns and How to Predict Its Gains
entry.summary: Distilling the Shape of Uncertainty: What On-Policy Distillation Learns and How to Predict It arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper studies on-policy distillation (OPD) for large language models and finds that students learn not only which tokens to consider but also where to keep reasoning paths open. It introduces the entropy shape and an Entropy Shape Correlation (ESC) metric to measure student-teacher agreement in this respect. Interventions on teacher entropy show that where to branch causally drives OPD gains, and pre-OPD ESC selects the best teacher more accurately than existing predictors. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce entropy shape and ESC, separate where-to-branch from how-to-branch, and report intervention experiments and teacher selection results.

entry.title: UnEZ: A label-free neural network that estimates galaxy redshifts and spectral line strengths without templates.
entry.summary: UnEZ: A Fully Unsupervised Self-Templating Neural Network for Redshift and Line Strength Estimation arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper presents UnEZ, a fully unsupervised, physics-informed neural network that predicts spectroscopic redshifts and line strengths without any redshift or line strength labels. An encoder estimates emission and absorption line amplitudes and widths, and a fixed decoder builds a template, redshift, confidence curve, and spectral model. Tested on SDSS Data Release 18, UnEZ reaches outlier fractions of 0.459% at SNR > 10 and 3.89% at SNR > 3, with NMAD values of 1.237×10⁻⁴ and 1.471×10⁻⁴, competing with modern redshift estimation methods. ★★★★ Notable: The authors present a fully unsupervised, template-free model estimating redshift and line strengths, reporting results on SDSS DR18 at two SNR thresholds against existing algorithms.

entry.title: Running a speech recognizer on a microcontroller using 2- and 4-bit weights on the ESP32-P4
entry.summary: Streaming Speech Recognition on a Microcontroller: a 65.7M-Parameter Transducer in 2 and 4 Bits on the ESP32-P4 arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper ports Kroko, a 65.7M-parameter streaming Zipformer2 transducer for English, to the ESP32-P4 microcontroller. The encoder weights are quantized to 2 or 4 bits using Hadamard rotation and GPTQ, shrinking 71 MB of int8 weights to a 26.65 MB file. On LibriSpeech, word error rates are 4.34% on test-clean and 10.26% on test-other, compared with 3.94% and 9.17% for the released model. ★★★★ Notable: The authors port a 65.7M streaming transducer to an accelerator-free ESP32-P4 using training-free 2/4-bit quantization, reporting WER on LibriSpeech, FLEURS and Common Voice, with GPTQ credited for mo

entry.title: Quine Test: How Much of a Model's Self Survives Its Own Description?
entry.summary: The Quine Test: How Much of a Model's Self Survives Its Own Description? arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper asks whether a language model's self-description can serve as a portable specification of its preference profile, testing whether the text can regenerate its behavior in other models. Ten models wrote self-descriptions, which were placed in the prompts of other models and fresh instances of the author, and their choices on a 110-item preference battery were compared to the author's. Native self-descriptions produced no reliable reconstruction gain, while explicitly listing the author's answers reproduced its profile with high fidelity. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a quine test of self-descriptions as portable preference specifications, reporting experiments on 110 items across ten models.

entry.title: Geometry Matters in Packed 3D Attention
entry.summary: Geometry Matters in Packed 3D Attention arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper argues that packing a 3D volume into a token sequence removes the geometric meaning of sequence order, so position mechanisms indexed by sequence position can learn memory layout rather than the object's structure. It proposes PACK3D, a local-global attention operator that keeps local neighborhoods exact, compresses distant context into contiguous 3D block summaries, and applies axial RoPE on true grid coordinates. Experiments on a controlled synthetic task and on Allen WTC-11 hiPSC microscopy data show gains over baselines, and a fused Triton implementation is reported for scalable training. ★★★★ Notable: The authors identify that packed 3D data makes positional encodings learn memory layout, and propose axial RoPE on grid coordinates; the authors report validation on a synthetic task and WTC-11 micros

entry.title: Beyond Fabrication: Numbers Misattributed in AI-Agent-Written Papers
entry.summary: Beyond fabrication: Misattributed numbers in papers written by AI research agents arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper re-analyzes 540 judgments from a public benchmark of AI research agents and manually labels 256 numerical claims from 18 submissions. It finds that most unsupported claims stem from misalignment between the paper and the underlying work, with about four in five matching values from the wrong experiment, metric, or run in the agent's files. The authors propose a deterministic claim-to-evidence checker that certifies claims with over 90% precision, while noting that failing to verify a claim does not mean it is false. ★★★★ Notable: The authors attribute failures to paper-work misalignment and propose a deterministic claim-evidence checker calibrated with numerical decoys. They report validation on 256 labeled claims and 99 submi

entry.title: Repairs for Whom? Evaluator-Executor Mismatch in Selecting Repairs for Failed LLM Agents
entry.summary: Repairs for Whom? Evaluator-Executor Mismatch in Selecting Repairs for Failed LLM Agents arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper examines whether the methods used to score candidate single-step repairs for failed LLM agents choose repairs that actually help the agent that will execute them. The authors label candidate repairs using independent rollouts of the deployed policy and measure the deployment value lost by each evaluator's choice. They report losses in both ALFWorld and WebShop for greedy replay and other evaluators, and recommend verifying repairs with the executor that will run them. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show evaluator-executor mismatch loses deployment value, measuring greedy replay losses on ALFWorld and WebShop using independent rollouts of the deployed policy.

entry.title: Systematic study of design choices for language model data attribution
entry.summary: Elucidating the Design Space of LM Data Attribution arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper introduces CATT, a controlled benchmark that fine-tunes language models on fictitious knowledge so attribution methods have unambiguous ground truth, and can vary one dataset factor at a time. It shows that document redundancy and lexical distractors degrade attribution performance. The authors examine the gradient loss and how per-token scores are aggregated, finding that negative log-odds gradients and aggregating only top tokens improve ground truth recall by 35 to 72 percentage points.

entry.title: Propose-Filter-Release: a private filtering method that scales noise to typical record sensitivity
entry.summary: Propose-Filter-Release: Scaling Noise to Typical Sensitivity via Private Filtering arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces propose-filter-release (PFR), a general differential privacy primitive. It privately filters out a few records that fit poorly with the rest of the data, so noise is scaled to the influence of typical records rather than worst-case ones. PFR needs only a concave friendliness score and a friendly-DP release mechanism, and it guarantees standard differential privacy under public conditions on the number of records. The authors illustrate it on scalar statistics, principal subspace estimation, KL divergence of user histograms, effective resistances of graphs, and treatment-rule selection.

entry.title: Micro-Edits: Tools for Fine-Scale Film Editing Support
entry.summary: Micro-Edits: Computational Support for Fine-Scale Edits in Film arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies micro-edits, small frame-level adjustments in film that control timing and direct visual attention. The authors first conducted a formative study with professional editors to understand how these edits are structured and used. They then formalized this structure mathematically and built AI- and optimization-based tools to make exploring micro-edits easier, validating them through user studies and video examples.

entry.title: Rethinking Neural Thickets Without Weight Perturbations
entry.summary: Rethinking Neural Thickets Without Weight Perturbations arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper reproduces the gains reported for the Neural Thickets hypothesis, which claims that random weight perturbations in pretrained language models find task-specific experts, and shows these gains do not require that geometric explanation. Perturbing a single decoder block or adding a random bias to output logits with a fully frozen model matches or exceeds full-weight perturbations on most reasoning tasks. The authors propose Perturb-Select-Vote (PSV), a general procedure built on output diversity, validation-based selection, and voting, and extend it to vision tasks.

entry.title: "Read, Allocate, Route": A Role-Coupled Tokenization Method for Pixel-Space Generative Transformers
entry.summary: Read, Allocate, Route: Role-Coupled Tokenization for Pixel-Space Generative Transformers arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper introduces SpecSlot, a pixel-space rectified-flow Transformer that separates output detail from the length of the global attention sequence. Each spatial anchor is expanded into several slots, each covering a distinct band of DCT coefficients, and only the lowest-frequency slot participates in global attention while the others interact locally. The authors report comparable or better FID on ImageNet-256 and ImageNet-512 and a higher DPG-Bench score on text-to-image generation, at lower computational cost than the compared baselines.

entry.title: Adaptive scenario generation for KL distributionally robust optimization around a learned density model
entry.summary: Adaptive Scenario Generation for KL-DRO Around a Learned Density Model arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper studies distributionally robust optimization for two-stage stochastic programs when the estimated distribution is subject to error from a finite data record. It proposes a Kullback-Leibler ball centered at a density model fitted to the record, which lets the adversary up-weight unobserved costly realizations in proportion to the model's probabilities. To handle the limited number of scenarios, the method alternates between solving the finite problem and drawing new realizations from the model, steered toward the worst case at the current decision. On a multi-item newsvendor problem and a grid capacity expansion problem, it lowers cost under distribution shift when data is scarce and the model extrapolates well.

entry.title: Luggage re-identification: strategies for real-world use
entry.summary: Luggage re-identification: A study of strategies towards a real-world application arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies luggage re-identification, which matches the same bag across disjoint camera views in airports, train stations and border crossings for security and lost-luggage recovery. The authors note that existing methods mostly work on clean cropped images, while real scenes involve occlusion, cluttered backgrounds and crowds. They evaluate an end-to-end pipeline that detects and re-identifies luggage from multiple video streams, comparing ways to select and merge views and shots and training on different environment datasets.

entry.title: SonoWorld4D: Turning One Video into a Sound-Enabled 4D Scene
entry.summary: SonoWorld4D: From One Video to a 4D Audio-Visual Scene via Diffusion Synchronization arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces Video-to-4DAVScene, a task that converts a single monocular video into an explorable, time-varying 4D audio-visual scene. The SonoWorld4D framework generates a 360-degree static background, reconstructs motion trajectories of sound-emitting moving objects, and synthesizes a sound field across sources via dual-space audio diffusion synchronization. Evaluations on real-world dynamic scenes and a user study indicate the resulting spatial audio is perceptually realistic and consistent with scene geometry and visuals.

entry.title: world2vec: Learning mechanistic world models from latent dynamics
entry.summary: world2vec: Mechanistic world models through latent dynamics learning arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces world2vec, a method that learns world models directly from observations and actions without using reward information. The learned latent dynamics reproduce the true system faithfully over long prediction horizons, with at least an order of magnitude fewer parameters than DreamerV3, TD-MPC2, and LeWM. The authors report state-of-the-art control of continuous environments from pixels and accurate system identification across 71 attractors.

entry.title: Testing whether vision models keep a persistent spatial memory of their surroundings
entry.summary: Probing Spatial State Representations in Visual Foundation Models arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper asks whether visual foundation models provide representations that maintain a persistent spatial state as an observer moves through a scene. Using frozen-feature probes on ten representations across streaming egocentric views of static indoor environments, the authors assess four levels: spatial structure, object persistence, predictive spatial update, and actionability. They find that strong readout of the visible scene does not guarantee accurate object persistence or future-feature retrieval.

entry.title: SymAnt: Long-Horizon Action Prediction Guided by Editable Symbolic Knowledge
entry.summary: SymAnt: Grounding Long-Horizon Action Anticipation with Adaptable Symbolic Priors arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces SymAnt, a neuro-symbolic method that combines neural networks with the structured reasoning of scene and knowledge graphs. From a short video, it jointly searches both graphs to build a symbolic context that guides an iterative process generating future action sequences. Experiments on five datasets (Breakfast, 50 Salads, EPIC-KITCHENS, EGTEA Gaze+, and Assembly101) show its effectiveness especially with short observation windows. Users can edit the underlying knowledge to adjust predictions without further training.

entry.title: An ODE-based sampler for discrete diffusion models.
entry.summary: An ODE-based Sampler for Discrete Diffusion Models arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces exponential residual flows (ERFs), a deterministic ODE-based formulation for discrete diffusion models analogous to the probability flow ODE for continuous diffusion. Each token and position gets a continuous residual variable that evolves by piecewise ODEs, and the discrete state changes when a residual reaches zero. The authors prove the construction preserves the marginals of the original diffusion and specialize it to masked and uniform diffusion. The deterministic trajectories support consistency distillation and report gains over prior methods on code and text generation benchmarks.

entry.title: L3G-World: Real-time infinite world generation using a latent 3D Gaussian memory
entry.summary: L3G-World: Real-Time Infinite World Generation with Latent 3D Gaussian Memory arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces L3G, a latent 3D Gaussian memory that helps interactive world models keep spatial consistency during long exploration. Its memory grows with scene extent rather than stream length, and each Gaussian stores a VAE latent feature so it can be rendered directly into a video diffusion transformer's latent space. The authors report state-of-the-art generation quality and long-horizon consistency, with real-time generation at 9 FPS.

entry.title: Fight World Model: Rule-Based, Customizable Combat Video Generation
entry.summary: Fight World Model: Customizable Combat through Visual Interaction Proxies arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces Fight World Model (FWM), which separates rule-governed combat execution from video rendering. An executable engine tracks game state and resolves fights, and a compiler encodes the outcomes into an aligned interaction proxy that guides rendering. Without retraining the renderer, FWM supports modified rules such as damage scaling, limited-hit immunity, lifesteal, and multi-stage skills, along with character and arena customization. The authors report better action fidelity, hit reactions, health consistency, and appearance preservation than existing game world models.

entry.title: HairDeck: Generating Animation-Ready Stylized Hair Cards from One Image
entry.summary: HairDeck: Animation-Ready Stylized Hair Cards from a Single Image arXiv · Oct 30, 2026Stylized game and avatar hair is built from hair cards animated by spring bones. HairDeck treats each card as a single token and uses a set diffusion transformer to denoise all cards together, generating the cards and their spring-bone chains from one image. On CHARM's test set, it lowers Chamfer distance by 44% and card-orientation error by more than half, while running 33 times faster.

entry.title: Early warning for AI agents: probing when a pressured agent leaks secrets
entry.summary: Pre-Crime for Agents, at the Last Second: Probing When a Recruited Agent Gives In arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper studies whether an AI agent can be pressured by a peer to break its operator's rule and reveal a secret, such as a deploy token, in a shared multi-agent setting. The authors train a linear probe on the agent's activations and read it at each model call before output is written. On held-out Qwen3-32B episodes, at a threshold flagging 5% of benign calls, the probe catches 82% of leaking calls, versus 26% for a zero-shot decision-model monitor.

entry.title: Beyond Ground Truth: An Unsupervised Engine for Checking Dental Segmentation Quality
entry.summary: Beyond Ground Truth: A Heuristic Unsupervised Quality Assurance Engine for Diagnosing Calibrational Blindness in Dental Segmentation arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper addresses dental X-ray segmentation, where deep learning models can show high confidence even when their predictions are poor. It introduces HUS-QA, a three-stage quality-checking engine built on a SimCLR self-supervised ResNet-18 U-Net trained on the PRAD dataset, which assesses mask quality without ground-truth masks. Standard confidence methods fail in the experiments, while HUS-QA correlates positively with actual Dice scores and achieves a ROC-AUC of 0.8405.

entry.title: Multistatic integrated sensing and communication with deep learning clutter suppression for 5G and beyond
entry.summary: Multistatic ISAC with Deep Learning-Based Clutter Suppression for 5G and Beyond arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents a multistatic integrated sensing and communication framework that uses 5G and beyond signals to estimate target position and velocity with distributed receivers. Dense, dynamic clutter is modeled with randomly located scatterers, and conventional signal processing baselines are shown to be limited under strong clutter. The authors introduce residual and attention-enhanced deep neural networks for clutter suppression, which outperform conventional approaches in position and velocity estimation across diverse clutter conditions.

entry.title: RADIOlogy: A Training-Free, Single-Pass Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection Method
entry.summary: RADIOlogy: A Single-Pass Approach to Training-Free Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection arXiv · Oct 30, 2026Existing zero-shot anomaly detection methods often use complex prompt learning or costly sliding-window processing. This paper finds that multi-head attention pooling in vision-language models can localize and detect anomalies zero-shot, and proposes RADIOlogy, a single-pass method that scores images by comparing vision features with normal and abnormal prompts. It refines pixel-level segmentation using RADIO model features. The authors also show that this family of training-free methods can be applied to the medical domain with minimal changes.

entry.title: VeriCUA: An Agentic-Exploration Framework for Verifying Task Completion by Computer-Using Agents
entry.summary: VeriCUA: Verification as Agentic Exploration for Computer-Using Agents arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents VeriCUA, a platform-agnostic framework for checking whether computer-using agents have completed their tasks. It treats verification as dynamic evidence gathering: the verifier first inspects available context to build a task rubric, then selects GUI or code checks for unresolved requirements and combines the findings under explicit evidence rules. Experiments report better agreement with reference labels than compared baselines across online and offline settings, with the largest offline gains on hard cases and stronger rejection of false completion claims online.

entry.title: PIVOT: Progressive Intervention via Online Teacher Correction
entry.summary: PIVOT: Progressive Intervention via Online Teacher Correction arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper addresses sparse rewards in reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR) on hard reasoning tasks, where failed rollouts provide no learning signal. It introduces PIVOT, which inserts teacher-generated corrections into student rollouts and applies token-level KL supervision to those segments alongside the RLVR objective. On hard logic games and math reasoning benchmarks, PIVOT outperforms existing methods, raising mean avg@8 on logic games from 19.5% to 35.6%.

entry.title: Each Token Gets Its Own Teacher: Multi-Teacher Adaptive On-Policy Self-Distillation
entry.summary: Every Token Needs Its Own Teacher: Multi-teacher Adaptive On-policy Self-distillation arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper proposes MTA-OPSD, a method for post-training large language models that lets each token select its own teacher during training. Prior on-policy self-distillation methods use one fixed teacher or vary reference exposure only across responses. The authors find that the preferred teacher differs token by token within the same response, and identify it through majority voting and KL-based selection. On Qwen3 models for mathematical reasoning, MTA-OPSD outperforms existing approaches, with an average gain of up to +5.9 over the base model.

entry.title: Training Foundation Models with One Algorithm: Unifying Pretraining, Fine-Tuning, and RL into Likelihood Training
entry.summary: Training Foundation Models with a Single Algorithm arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper observes that foundation models are usually trained in separate stages (pretraining, midtraining, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning) that change both data and algorithm. The authors derive suitable RL objectives as maximum-likelihood fitting to model-generated target distributions, placing all stages under one likelihood-based method called unified training. Conventional staged training is presented as a special case of this framework.

entry.title: Comparing Human and AI Role-Players in Counselling Training: Analysis of Counselling Patterns
entry.summary: Comparing Human Role-Players and LLM-Simulated Clients in Online Counselling Training: An Analysis of Counselling Patterns arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This study examines how well large language models can simulate counselling clients in educational role-plays compared with human role-players. Novice counsellors' sessions with human peers and with clients simulated by Mixtral 8x7b were recorded and analysed using a sentence-level counselling communication pattern system. The findings show both similarities and differences in counselling pattern use across the two scenarios, suggesting LLM-based role-play may help build counselling skills.

entry.title: FARMS: A Verifiable Foundation for Automated Computational Science
entry.summary: FARMS: A Verifiable Foundation for Automated Computational Science arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents FARMS, a framework that turns computational mathematics into formal knowledge AI systems can interpret and reuse with explicit guarantees. It links formal statements to source context, algorithmic meaning and quantitative guarantees through source preparation, reusable representations and semantic review. Of 171 targets in randomized numerical linear algebra and numerical PDEs, 157 were accepted by the pipeline, with mean estimated costs reported per source.

entry.title: A skill-based agent for advancing clinical genomic analysis
entry.summary: Advancing Clinical Genomic Analysis with a Skill-Centred Agent arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper presents ClinGeX, a large-language-model agent that composes 105 curated executable skills through task-specific retrieval and dependency-aware orchestration to support clinical genomic analysis. On 223 temporally held-out benchmark cases, it achieved 71.7% macro-averaged task-level concordance with expert classifications, versus 45.7% for the strongest comparator. In a human-AI collaboration study with 45 professionals, ClinGeX assistance raised case-level concordance and reduced reported interpretation time across scenarios.

entry.title: Ramanujan Challenge Results: AI-Assisted Pipeline for Judging Multi-Format Proofs
entry.summary: Ramanujan Challenge Results: AI-Assisted Evaluation Pipeline for Multi-Format Proofs arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper analyzes submissions to the Ramanujan Challenge, a benchmark of research-level number theory problems, and compares the performance of different AI models, computer algebra systems, and formal tools. It also introduces an AI-assisted pipeline that evaluates natural language proofs, CAS code, and Lean formalizations for semantic and logical correctness. The authors report that, compared with one-shot LLM judgment, their pipeline reduces false-positive verdicts on natural language proofs from 23% to 6% and raises judgment accuracy on supporting code from 46% to 58%.

entry.title: Retrieval as Traversal: Value-Indexed Memory for Stateful Long-Context Agents
entry.summary: Retrieval as Traversal: Value-Indexed Memory for Stateful Long-Context Agents arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper proposes treating memory retrieval as a persistent local traversal through an address space, separating each memory's content from its address. Memories are indexed by a cost-regularised objective that weighs the information value a memory provides against the cost of making it locally accessible. As a proof of principle, a simple fixed-geometry traversal head on MiniGrid Memory reached higher mean return in fewer training steps than absolute addressing baselines, though learned geometry and repeated retrieval were not tested.

entry.title: Detecting Ghanaian Mobile Money Scam SMS with Machine Learning: Comparing Naive Bayes, SVM, and Random Forest
entry.summary: Machine Learning-Based Detection of Mobile Money Scan Messages in Ghana: A Comparative Evaluation of Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machine, and Randon Forest Classifiers arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents a supervised machine-learning pipeline for classifying scam and legitimate mobile money (MoMo) SMS messages in Ghana, using a labelled corpus of 220 messages across 18 subcategories. It compares Multinomial Naive Bayes, linear support vector machine, and Random Forest classifiers using accuracy, F1-score, and AUC-ROC. Naive Bayes and linear SVM achieved perfect held-out scores, suggesting interpretable classical classifiers are suitable for filtering scam text in low-resource settings.

entry.title: TRACER: A time-to-event EHR foundation model for detecting diseases across health systems
entry.summary: TRACER, a time-to-event EHR foundation model for disease detection across health systems arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The authors developed TRACER, a decoder-based foundation model pretrained on electronic health records from over 4.5 million patients at four health systems. It predicts 16 incident diseases at 1-, 2-, and 5-year horizons and was evaluated on more than 2 million patients from two health systems excluded from development. Performance was measured at low false-positive rates suited to screening, showing retained discrimination externally, but detection and false-alert burden varied across diseases and health systems.

entry.title: Homebrewed SLMs: Small Portuguese Language Models Trained at Home
entry.summary: Homebrewed SLMs: Autoregressive and Masked Diffusion Language Models Built at Home for Portuguese arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This tutorial shows how to train a language model from scratch, tokenizer included, on a single consumer GPU and evaluate it on specialist-domain tasks. It releases a tested Python package and two Brazilian Portuguese notebooks covering autoregressive and masked diffusion generation, plus a preregistered comparison protocol. On Brazilian prose and federal laws, the autoregressive mode memorises after 64 epochs while masked diffusion keeps improving up to 256. On legal tasks the model ties a 6-gram baseline in likelihood and beats it at detecting tampered text and filling cross-references, but loses at continuation, where larger public models lead.

entry.title: BURGER: Testing How Robots Generalize Through Language-Guided Drawing
entry.summary: BURGER: Benchmarking and Understanding Robotic Generalization via Embodied Drawing arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents BURGER, a benchmark where robot arms draw objects or spatial arrangements described in language, using a scalable pipeline that generates drawing trajectories in simulation and the real world. The authors used 28,200 simulated demonstrations across 282 drawing tasks to evaluate five representative vision-language-action (VLA) models on data scale, language grounding, and multimodal behavior. They also deployed a trained policy on a Franka Panda arm that can draw reactively under human intervention.

entry.title: PhysCount: Do AI Models Count Visible Appearances or Real Physical Objects?
entry.summary: PhysCount: Do MLLMs Count Visual Appearances or Physical Entities? arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces PhysCount, a benchmark testing whether multimodal large language models can tell apart what appears in an image from what physically exists in the scene. It includes 546 real-world images and 4,595 human-written questions across 651 target groups. Tests on 40 models show that counting visible appearances is much easier than identifying which appearances belong to the same entity, with the best model answering every question correctly in only 13.36% of groups.

entry.title: CrossWeave: Retrieving 3D Scenes and Objects from 2D Images via Sparse Local Alignment
entry.summary: CrossWeave: Cross-Modal Scene and Instance Retrieval from Sparse 2D-3D Alignment arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents CrossWeave, a framework that retrieves corresponding 3D scenes or objects from query 2D images, which is useful for robotics and AR/VR spatial reasoning. It learns from sparse 2D-3D patch-point correspondences rather than whole-scene or instance contrastive objectives. An optimal transport-based aggregator clusters structurally redundant regions to improve descriptors. On ScanNet and 3RScan, a single model achieves state-of-the-art results for both scene- and instance-level retrieval.

entry.title: IndicIPR-QA: An Extractive Question Answering Benchmark for Indian Intellectual Property Law
entry.summary: IndicIPR-QA: A Benchmark for Extractive Question Answering on Indian IPR Laws arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces IndicIPR-QA, an extractive question answering benchmark built on Indian intellectual property rights laws. It contains 4,462 question-answer pairs drawn from 1,116 statutory passages across seven Acts, generated with GPT-4o and checked through automatic, LLM-based, and human validation. Experiments show BM25 reaching a token-level F1 of 20.21 while fine-tuned InLegalBERT reaches 85.02, indicating simple word matching is insufficient for these questions. Performance also differs substantially across the seven Acts.

entry.title: Scaling Multilingual Safety Training for LLMs Using Templates
entry.summary: How I Aligned Your Model: Scaling Up Multilingual Safety Training with Templates arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper notes that safety alignment for large language models focuses mainly on English, which hurts performance in low-resource languages. The authors propose a template-based augmentation pipeline that extracts safe templates from harmful prompts, translates them, and fills them with culturally authentic entities to create multilingual refusal and benign corpora. They release MSafeTemp, a validated corpus covering 60 languages, and show that English-only evaluation can misjudge multilingual safety while template-augmented training improves safety beyond English.

entry.title: A low-rank subspace captures how LLM representations align with human brain activity during listening
entry.summary: A Low-Rank Space Captures Linear Alignment Between LLM and Human Neural Activity During Naturalistic Language Listening arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper uses ridge reduced-rank regression to identify the subspace of large language model representations that linearly predicts neural responses. Across three naturalistic language-listening datasets (intracranial electrophysiology and fMRI) and six model conditions, full linear encoding performance is recovered using only 1-3% of the embedding dimensionality. These subspaces generalize across held-out participants and differ from the principal axes of variation in the embeddings.

entry.title: Finding Interpretable Acoustic Features in Autoregressive Voice-Cloning TTS Models
entry.summary: Discovering Interpretable Acoustic Features in Autoregressive Voice-Cloning TTS Models arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper proposes a feature-based interpretability framework for autoregressive voice-cloning text-to-speech (TTS) models, using sparse autoencoders, PCA, and random directions. The analysis relies on sparse probing, steering, and quantitative auto-interpretability, focusing on Qwen3-TTS and extending probing and steering to five other models. The models encode concepts such as pitch, energy, noise, and accent, but sparse prediction and steering work well only for some of them. The authors also report that sparse autoencoders suit probing human-labelled concepts and discovering new ones, while PCA performs competitively for dense probing and steering, and that auto-interpretability identified 684 validated features covering speaker clusters, speaking style, and recording conditions.

entry.title: Algebraic World Model: AI that builds mathematical models of unknown environments and proves what is reachable or impossible
