entry.summary: Algebraic World Model: From Exploration to Proofs arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper introduces the Algebraic World Model (AWM), a framework that explores unfamiliar environments, builds executable Python hypotheses, and formalizes the resulting model in Lean 4. AWM produces machine-checked proofs that certain goals are unreachable, including in two impossible game levels where baseline coding-tool models produced none. Across the 25 public ARC-AGI-3 games, the authors report that the models let Lean replay the winning trajectories of all 183 levels and predict unseen transitions.

entry.title: Numerical integration over bounded domains using learned reflected diffusions
entry.summary: Numerical Integration on Bounded Domains via Learned Reflected Diffusions arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies high-dimensional integration of a non-negative function over bounded convex domains, estimating the integral while keeping samples inside the domain. The authors build an importance-sampling proposal from reflected diffusion dynamics and train a neural score model to reverse a process that moves the target toward the uniform distribution on the domain. They derive a training objective without extra boundary terms, an unbiased integral estimator, and a REINFORCE-based gradient estimator for non-smooth integrands.

entry.title: LucidLyra: Feed-forward 3D scene generation with built-in semantic understanding
entry.summary: LucidLyra: Feed-Forward Generative 3D Scene Reconstruction and Joint Understanding via Multi-Task Distillation arXiv · Oct 30, 2026LucidLyra is a framework that generates 3D scenes from video latents in a single feed-forward pass, making them directly queryable for semantics and object instances. It distills knowledge from a camera-controlled video diffusion model and frozen 2D vision foundation models into one model that jointly predicts 3D Gaussians encoding geometry, appearance, open-vocabulary semantics, and class-agnostic instance cues. The method needs no per-scene optimization or 3D annotations and extends to monocular video for dynamic scenes.

entry.title: AI in EGI's e-infrastructure: past experience and future strategy
entry.summary: AI in the EGI e-infrastructure -- Past experiences and future strategies arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The EGI Federation has provided federated e-infrastructure services to science for over 15 years. This paper reviews EGI's early AI work in the interTwin and iMagine Horizon Europe projects, and notes that since 2023 the focus of AI in science has shifted from model training to adapting it to specific domains and questions. It then presents an AI strategy within the EGI Federation Strategy 2026-2030, built on three enablers: AI-ready infrastructure, human skills, and trust.

entry.title: Agentic University: Collaborative Agents for Personalized Learning
entry.summary: Agentic University: Collaborative Agents for Personalized Learning arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper introduces Human-Participatory Multi-Agent Organization and its implementation, Agentic University (AU), where learners work with specialized agents as organization members. Together they maintain a revisable Capability Program that links personal goals, multimodal learning activities, and layered assessment, adjusting support based on learner feedback and performance. Evaluation reports larger mean assessment gains (12.19 vs. 5.61 points on a 50-point scale) and stronger cognitive support for users.

entry.title: rTaste: Do Research Agents Have Taste? Judging Which Early Experiments to Run
entry.summary: rTaste: Do Research Agents Have Taste? Evaluating Early Stage Research Judgment arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper tests whether AI research agents can judge which experiments are worth running before their results are known. Six frontier models, working alone or in teams, proposed minimum viable experiments for seven recent NLP papers, forecast their outcomes and ranked them, and a separate executor ran all of them for review by three model auditors. Of 415 proposed experiments, 194 were judged sound, valuable and new, but only 73 were also judged beyond the seed paper and non-obvious. The agents' rankings showed limited improvement, and their forecasts were not measurably more accurate than a fresh instance of the same model.

entry.title: MetaRefine: Refining Image Quality Scores Using Multi-Level Features and Original Image Geometry
entry.summary: MetaRefine: Score Refinement with Multi-Level Features for Image Assessment arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces MetaRefine, a score refinement architecture that uses lightweight residual heads to correct scores from a frozen image assessment model. The corrections are predicted from original image geometry, multi-level visual features, and the model's original score, without changing the original scoring pipeline. Across 100 configurations on 21 datasets, it improves PLCC and SRCC in most configurations and reduces MAE and RMSE, with a median parameter overhead of only 1.11%, and it can further improve state-of-the-art models.

entry.title: The Precision Wall: A Boundary Where Optimizers Stall on Power-Law Measurement Spectra
entry.summary: The Precision Wall: An Optimizer-Dependent Boundary for Optimization under Power-Law Measurement Spectra arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies low-rank matrix sensing, where replacing isotropic Gaussian measurements with power-law covariances causes division-normalised first-order optimizers to stall above a critical exponent. The authors attribute the failure to a numerical precision limit: the smallest non-gauge expected Hessian eigenvalue decays with dimension, and once it falls below the optimizer's denominator floor, normalisation noise overwhelms rare-direction gradients. They give a leading-order boundary formula that predicts Adam's onset within 0.45 across a held-out grid of 16 configurations.

entry.title: Keeping LLMs Useful While Repeatedly Removing Training Data via Orthogonal Projection
entry.summary: Preserving Utility in Continual LLM Unlearning via Orthogonal Projections arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces Continual Orthogonal Projection (COP), a method for removing the influence of sensitive training data from large language models through repeated unlearning requests without retraining from scratch. Each update is restricted to the orthogonal complement of activation subspaces cached from earlier forget sets, storing only a low-rank basis per layer. Experiments on the TOFU and RWKU benchmarks show that COP preserves utility across sequential requests and forgets more effectively than continual-unlearning baselines.

entry.title: FIRME: A Memory Graph Anchored to a Registry for Evolving Investor Knowledge
entry.summary: FIRME: Registry-Anchored Memory Graphs for Evolving, Heterogeneous Investor Knowledge arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper introduces FIRME, a registry-anchored memory graph that links observations from investor calls, cash-flow records, and S&P 500 earnings-call transcripts to persistent canonical relationships while keeping source, time, and context. Persistent aliases direct recurring observations to the same relationship history across periods. Compared with a baseline that lacks alias memory, FIRME raises final-period Correct Match Rate by 7.8 to 12.1 percentage points across four dataset-backend settings.

entry.title: AVPS-360: A spatial audio-visual benchmark for segmenting and tracking sound-producing people
entry.summary: AVPS-360: A Spatial Audio-Visual Benchmark for Instance Segmentation and Tracking of Sound-Producing Persons arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces AVPS-360, a benchmark for segmenting and tracking people who produce sound in 360-degree videos, using first-order Ambisonics spatial audio. Built on STARSS23, it contains 230 recordings totaling 10.5 hours, with 31,678 manually reviewed instance masks linked to sound-event labels. The authors also propose a baseline that combines spatial audio and visual features, which they report substantially outperforms existing methods on long recordings with intermittent sound.

entry.title: MRI-free PET quantification using CT-to-MRI synthesis with reliability estimates
entry.summary: Accurate MRI-free PET Quantification and Reliability Assessment via CT-to-MRI Synthesis and Conformal Prediction arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper addresses amyloid PET SUVR quantification, which normally requires a subject's own T1-weighted MRI that is not always available. The authors synthesize MRI from CT using a diffusion model and apply conformal prediction to estimate a plausible range for the real MRI-based SUVR. On OASIS-3 11C-PiB PET, synthetic-MRI cortical SUVR closely matched real-MRI results and gave the same amyloid-positivity call in all 87 test subjects. Zero-shot testing on an external cohort worked without retraining, though conformal calibration needed recalibration on the target cohort.

entry.title: Training AI chatbots in simulated settings to conduct psychiatric intake interviews
entry.summary: Training language models in simulation for psychiatric intake arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper trains language models with multi-turn reinforcement learning in simulated environments to improve structured text-based psychiatric intake, covering history-taking, differential diagnosis, and initial management planning. In a randomized, double-blind crossover study, 32 psychiatrists role-played standardized patients and 15 separate psychiatrists scored the transcripts. The trained agent outperformed its base model in 76.7% of matched scenario pairs and more than halved under-triage of acute safety risks.

entry.title: Nonlinear dynamical systems as efficient physical neural networks
entry.summary: Nonlinear Dynamical Systems as Scalable and Efficient Physical Neural Networks arXiv · Oct 16, 2026This paper studies using nonlinear dynamical systems as physical neural networks that perform machine-learning inference with high energy efficiency. In simulations, applying modern training practices such as model compression lets these systems reach 99.2% accuracy on MNIST handwritten-digit recognition. A parameter-efficient architecture inspired by MLP-Mixers reaches up to 86.4% on CIFAR-10 with over 5 times fewer trainable parameters than the baseline. The authors give back-of-the-envelope estimates suggesting energy efficiency and speed gains of orders of magnitude over digital electronic neural networks may be possible.

entry.title: Rural Readiness: Domain generalization when the hard domains are chosen adversarially
entry.summary: Rural Readiness: Domain Generalization with Adversarially Chosen Domains arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper studies how a model trained on several source domains can perform on any unseen target domain, aiming to match the worst hypothesis consistent with the source data. It characterizes the sample complexity of this goal up to logarithmic factors. Relaxing the goal to compete with hypotheses that do well on 99% rather than 100% of source domains reduces the sample complexity from Ω(dk) to O(d), where d is the VC dimension and k the number of source domains.

entry.title: InfantNet: A large dataset for estimating infant body pose and shape
entry.summary: InfantNet: A Large Scale Dataset for Infant Body Pose and Shape Estimation arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces InfantNet, the largest real-image dataset of infants to date, with 108,902 RGB images of infants aged 6 to 18 months. Every image has 2D keypoint annotations, and 11,642 images also include 3D pose and shape labels with full SMIL parameters. Baseline experiments show that adult pose estimators generalize poorly to infants, but fine-tuning on InfantNet gives consistent improvements.

entry.title: A shared benchmark for aerial-enhanced self-driving: the KITScenes Aerial dataset
entry.summary: A Unified Benchmark for Aerial-Enhanced Autonomous Driving: The KITScenes Aerial Dataset arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces KITScenes Aerial, an extension of the KITScenes Multimodal dataset that adds synchronized aerial imagery and higher-resolution neural representations. It provides a common basis for map construction, aerial-assisted online HD mapping, and cross-view localization. Mapping is evaluated across all 53 map classes, showing that aerial context especially helps fine-grained, extended-range mapping and that higher resolution improves results further. Under geographically disjoint conditions, cross-view localization achieves a mean translation error of 5.13 m.

entry.title: Glance: A Generator That Also Ranks Search Results
entry.summary: Glance: The Generator Is Its Own Reranker arXiv · Oct 30, 2026Retrieval-augmented generation usually runs separate models for reranking and answering, duplicating model memory and passage processing. Glance adds a lightweight decision adapter and pointer head to the generator, scoring candidate passages from one shared prefill without encoding each query-passage pair separately. Using a single 9B backbone fine-tuned on MS MARCO for about 39 minutes, it outperforms bge-reranker-v2-m3 on SciFact and NFCorpus in nDCG@10.

entry.title: PhysInsert: Physically Plausible Object Insertion with Geometric Priors
entry.summary: PhysInsert: Physically Plausible Object Insertion with Geometric Priors and Bidirectional Object-Scene Interactions arXiv · Oct 30, 2026PhysInsert is a framework for inserting objects into images based on a reference, adjusting both the object and its surrounding scene so the result looks physically plausible. The authors build the Insert World dataset of strictly aligned Blender-rendered counterfactual pairs across viewpoints and lighting, and add geometry-guided adaptation with 2D object-scene spatial supervision. They also introduce the PhysInsert-Bench benchmark, and experiments on it and DreamBooth show improved image fidelity, while a user study reports better placement, lighting integration, perspective, and pose plausibility.

entry.title: A review of reinforcement learning for controlling partial differential equations
entry.summary: Reinforcement learning for control of partial differential equations arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This review connects reinforcement learning with PDE-constrained optimization, surveying model-free, model-based, and multi-agent approaches to controlling systems governed by partial differential equations. It emphasizes sample efficiency, generalization across parametric variations, and scalability to high-dimensional problems. Two examples, stabilizing a chaotic system and a flow control problem, illustrate the performance and pitfalls of RL agents, and the paper discusses evaluation practices, current limitations, and open research directions.

entry.title: Learning cell development dynamics using family tree information
entry.summary: Learning developmental dynamics from lineage context arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces lineage inpainting, a generative model that uses information about a cell's relatives, such as sisters and cousins, to predict how cell states change across lineage trees. It combines tree-structured transformers with stochastic interpolants. Applied to a lineage-traced transcriptional atlas of mouse embryogenesis, the model recovers dynamics that gene expression alone does not reveal, including cases where distinct lineages converge to a common state. Trained only on unperturbed development, it can also simulate counterfactuals to generate hypotheses about perturbation responses, and in many cases these agree with observed phenotypes, including a Tbx5 knockout measurement.

entry.title: Prefix Executability: Judging Tool-Using AI Agents by Each Step, Not Just the End Result
entry.summary: Prefix Executability: Evaluating Tool-Using Agents Beyond Final Success arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper argues that tool-use benchmarks scoring only final task success can hide whether an agent's intermediate tool-call sequence was actually executable. It proposes a prefix executability protocol that checks whether every prefix of a predicted tool-call sequence stays valid under tool schemas, state preconditions, and data dependencies, summarized with several reliability metrics. Experiments on BFCL-v3, ToolSandbox, and τ³-bench show that rankings based on final success diverge from prefix-level rankings.

entry.title: Framework-constrained generative model for discovering new inorganic crystal materials
entry.summary: Framework-Conditional Open Materials Generation arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces OMatG-FC, a generative method for de novo inorganic crystal materials that is constrained by known structural frameworks, meaning unit cell shapes and particle positions. It uses discrete flow matching for atomic species and stochastic interpolants for unit cell volume scaling, which reduces the problem's dimensionality. The authors also analyze duplicate frameworks in the MP-20 dataset and report state-of-the-art stable, unique, and novel rates on LeMat-GenBench.

entry.title: A pretrained model that filters noisy signals across different dynamical systems
entry.summary: A Pretrained Model for Bayesian Filtering in Heterogeneous Dynamical Systems arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper introduces FilterFM, the first pretrained model for Bayesian filtering, which estimates latent states across heterogeneous dynamical systems using a single checkpoint. It uses a hierarchical two-level observation sequence encoder and a prior-to-posterior state-reconstruction module, and models uncertainty via quantile prediction. Reported results show gains in in-domain accuracy, runtime, and noise robustness over baselines, along with the first zero-shot filtering on unseen dynamics.

entry.title: Soil moisture estimation for farming using knowledge distillation from simpler single-input models
entry.summary: Soil Moisture Estimation in Precision Agriculture: A Knowledge Distillation Approach arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper proposes Soil Moisture Distillation (SMD), a knowledge distillation framework that uses unimodal teacher models to improve multimodal soil moisture estimation. It also finds that crop images provide better visual cues than soil patches. SMD improves MAPE by 2% for soil patches and 1.2% for crops over state-of-the-art baselines.

entry.title: Adaptive Search with Path-Constrained Mobile Sensors Using Multi-Armed Bandits: A method for energy-limited sensor teams to choose routes adaptively to find regions of interest.
entry.summary: Adaptive search with path-constrained mobile sensors using multi-arm bandits arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper studies how a team of energy-limited mobile sensors can detect regions of interest from noisy online measurements. Sensors move only along precomputed feasible paths that respect mobility limits, require returning to charging stations, and avoid known obstacles. The authors model path selection as a multi-armed bandit problem and propose an iterative search algorithm based on confidence bounds, with finite-time and anytime probabilistic correctness guarantees and non-asymptotic bounds on detection and labeling times.

entry.title: Uncertainty-aware feedback loop diagnosis combining reinforcement learning and conformal prediction for wafer defect classification
entry.summary: Uncertainty-aware Feedback Loop Diagnosis: integrating reinforcement learning and conformal prediction for reliable wafer defect classification arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper proposes UFLD, an algorithm for detecting defects in wafer maps. It uses reinforcement learning to adaptively choose measurements and reports a prediction uncertainty level after each step, stopping once enough information is obtained. The method uses conformal prediction to set the stopping time, without needing a separate learned confidence network. On the MixedWM38 dataset, UFLD reduces acquisition time by about 40% and reaches 98.4% inspection accuracy.

entry.title: NECA: Borrowing Event Timing from Similar ICU Patients to Predict Organ Dysfunction
entry.summary: NECA: Neighbor Event Curve Augmentation for Multi-Horizon ICU Deterioration Prediction arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper proposes NECA, a model-agnostic method that finds training patients with similar early ICU records and converts their later organ dysfunction event onset times into cumulative event-curve features over 6, 12, 24, and 42 hours. These features are appended to each patient's representation and fed to standard predictors. On PhysioNet 2012 and a 4,000-stay MIMIC-IV subset, NECA improves average PR-AUC and ROC-AUC across four organ dysfunction event tasks, with the largest gain for neurological dysfunction.

entry.title: IMPACT: Inverter-Informed Multimodal Learning for Photovoltaic Power Forecasting
entry.summary: IMPACT: Inverter-Informed Multimodal Learning for Photovoltaic Generation Forecasting arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents a physics-informed multimodal deep learning framework for probabilistic photovoltaic power forecasts 10 to 110 minutes ahead. It combines plant-level temporal history, inverter-level spatial cloud dynamics, solar geometry, and current weather through gated cross-attention, with online conformal calibration of quantile outputs. The model outperforms all 14 baselines in forecast skill score, and retains useful skill under overcast and variable sky conditions.

entry.title: OCCAMS: A Multi-Task Learning Study of CMB Power Spectra
entry.summary: OCCAMS: A Multi-Task Learning-Based Investigation of the CMB Power Spectra arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper uses multi-task learning with variational autoencoders, without any built-in cosmological model, to fit the cosmic microwave background temperature and polarisation power spectra with a small number of latent variables. Compared with Planck 2018 data, six latent variables give the best or near-best fit, matching the number of free parameters in the standard model-dependent approach. The latent variables correspond partly to standard cosmological parameters, suggesting that deep learning can provide a compact, data-driven parametrisation of CMB spectra.

entry.title: Linking hidden neurons in audio classifiers to human-understandable acoustic concepts.
entry.summary: Bridging Neural Representations and Symbolic Semantics in Audio Classification arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper examines whether hidden neurons in deep audio classifiers can be linked to human-understandable symbolic acoustic concepts. It presents a model-agnostic neurosymbolic framework that uses symbolic concept induction to analyze the final 32-neuron hidden layer. The framework is tested on music genre classification with GTZAN and musical instrument classification with IRMAS. Several neurons were associated with meaningful concepts, and most confirmed pairs were statistically supported by the Mann-Whitney U test.

entry.title: Retrieving from Your Own Mistakes: On-Policy Training of Embedding Models for Multi-Hop Retrieval-Augmented Generation
entry.summary: Retrieving from Your Own Mistakes: On-Policy Training of Embedding Models for Multi-Hop Retrieval-Augmented Generation arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper addresses multi-hop retrieval-augmented generation, where answers need evidence spread across several documents. It finds that chain embedding retrievers trained only on gold histories perform strongly, but their mistakes at test time reduce their ability to find missing evidence. The authors propose on-policy state training, which trains the encoder on the states it reaches itself, and report that this retrieves complete evidence more often and transfers to harder long-chain variants.

entry.title: Continuous-Action World Models for Transferring Robot Dynamics Across Embodiments
entry.summary: Continuous-Action World Models: Learning Cross-Embodiment Spatiotemporal Dynamics Priors arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces Continuous-Action World Models (CoAWM), a framework that learns spatiotemporal dynamics priors usable across different robot embodiments and control frequencies. It uses a shared latent function space, first pretrained on trajectories from heterogeneous robots and sampling rates, then connected to a world-model backbone that conditions on observations, language, and robot state. A single decoder returns end-effector actions at any queried time.

entry.title: Scaling math proof training data using structured textbooks
entry.summary: Scaling Mathematical Proof Supervision from Structured Textbooks arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces TOME-Math, a corpus converting 2,118 university mathematics textbooks into about 380K structured proof-supervision records that keep chapter order, proposition-proof links, dependency references, and source provenance. The authors use these structural signals to explore curriculum learning across mathematical subjects and to study scaling with supervision volume and source breadth. At full scale, the paper reports that fine-tuning on TOME-Math raises the unweighted mean score by 16.7 percentage points over the base model and exceeds three public instruction-data baselines in aggregate.

entry.title: Combining and guiding several diffusion models with a generalized Feynman-Kac correction method
entry.summary: Composing and Steering Diffusion Models with Generalized Feynman-Kac Correctors arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces generalized Feynman-Kac correctors (GFKC), a framework for sampling from an arbitrary target function defined over several pretrained diffusion models. The authors show that geometric interpolation between an initial function and the target satisfies a Feynman-Kac PDE and derive its potential in closed form. The method runs in the log domain, supports reward-based steering, and corrects generation on the fly without retraining. It is validated on analytic Gaussian models and on diffusion models trained on MNIST.

entry.title: Testing AI language models on randomly chosen unsolved math conjectures
entry.summary: Beyond Selected Breakthroughs: Evaluating Language Models on Randomly Sampled Mathematical Conjectures arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The authors introduce OpenConjecture, a dataset of conjectures from arXiv mathematics papers published since February 2026. Frontier GPT models were applied to 200 randomly sampled conjectures over three passes, producing candidate solutions for roughly 60% of them, with counterexamples about 1.3 times more common than proofs. The paper also examines solution novelty, literature citation, and whether resolutions rely on errors or underspecification in the conjecture.

entry.title: LLM agent reasoning for predicting pediatric diabetes outcomes from multimodal medical records
entry.summary: Agentic LLM reasoning in pediatric diabetes outcome prediction from multimodal medical records arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper tests large language model agents for clinical prediction in children, using records from 2,489 youths with type 2 diabetes and 4,018 with type 1 diabetes. Data included structured records, social determinants from clinical notes, and glucose monitoring data for type 1 patients. Using 18 months of follow-up, the authors predicted seven type 2 diabetes outcomes at 24 months. The evidence-citing CEDAR pipeline outperformed trained machine learning models in both cohorts, and two pediatric endocrinologists reached the same prediction as CEDAR in about nine of ten cases.

entry.title: HiFOR: Hierarchical Foresight for Robot Vision-Language-Action Models
entry.summary: HiFOR: Hierarchical Foresight with Action-Guided World Grounding for Vision-Language-Action Model arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper proposes HiFOR, a framework for vision-language-action robot models that predicts future states at multiple time scales. A Hierarchical Dependency Mask jointly predicts short-term state changes, semantic milestones, and final goal states. The method organizes future latent representations along time, view, and spatial dimensions, and retrieves relevant future information guided by evolving action representations during denoising. Experiments were conducted on two simulation benchmarks and six real-world robotic manipulation tasks.

entry.title: The Athlete as a Scientist of One: Agentic Bayesian Experimental Design for Individualized Physiology from Consumer Wearables
entry.summary: The Athlete as a Scientist of One: Agentic Bayesian Experimental Design for Individualized Physiology from Consumer Wearables arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents EpiCoach, an agentic system that studies one cross-country mountain biker as an auditable N-of-1 experiment. Claims about the athlete are kept in an evidence-gated registry, each requiring a probabilistic prediction before a session and updated only through logged statistical fits. Predictions come from a digital twin built from heart rate, GPS and barometric altitude, and the agent designs each next training week as a constrained experiment. Evaluated on eighteen months of data via replay benchmarks and a live prospective phase, the authors release the registry, benchmark and protocol.

entry.title: Curriculum or Easy Start? A Benchmark of Unsupervised Environment Design for Quadrupeds
entry.summary: Is It the Curriculum or Just the Easy Start? Benchmarking Unsupervised Environment Design on Quadrupeds arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper proposes a benchmark that compares 14 unsupervised environment design, domain randomisation and robotics curriculum methods under one protocol on five 3D quadrupeds in MuJoCo MJX. Terrains are described by eight interpretable parameters, and all curricula train the same PPO student with matched environment-step budgets. No method ranks in the top group on every robot and level set, and methods with easier training levels often lead on in-distribution random terrains. On three robots the leader on random levels differs from the leader on held-out terrain.

entry.title: Your LR Schedule May Not Be Principled: Effective Learning Rate Scheduling in Weight-Normalized Training
entry.summary: Your LR Schedule May Not Be Principled: Effective Learning Rate Scheduling in Weight-Normalized Training arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper argues that the pretraining loss gains of weight-normalized training mainly come from its effective learning rate trajectory rather than from normalization alone. It proposes AIR (Affine Inverse-square-Root decay), a schedule combining a 1/√t decay with an affine adjustment to meet set peak and terminal learning rates. In 128B-token Mixture-of-Experts pretraining, AIR reduces terminal training loss by about 0.01 relative to cosine, and applying the same effective learning rate trajectory to weight decay reproduces similar training dynamics.

entry.title: Don't Lose the Thread: Making LLM Agents Manage Their Own Memory on Long Tasks
entry.summary: Don't Lose the Thread: Empowering Long-Horizon LLM Agents with Cognitive Resource Self-Allocation arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper addresses LLM agents' struggles on long-horizon tasks, where cluttered working memory dilutes attention and hinders planning. It proposes CORAL, a paradigm in which agents checkpoint task progress and verified facts, then reset cluttered context and resume from a clean state, trained with a multi-episode reinforcement learning algorithm. On the GAIA benchmark, an 8B model with CORAL reaches 42.8% average accuracy, using 6-7 times fewer input tokens than a ReAct agent.

entry.title: A unified Hessian-guided method for post-training quantization of language models
entry.summary: A Unified Hessian-Guided Framework for Post-Training Quantization arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper proposes a unified framework for post-training quantization of large language models. Using a tractable Fisher approximation, it derives a Hessian-guided estimate of the output change caused by joint weight and activation quantization. The method jointly optimizes quantization ranges, linear transformations, and weight rounding under a shared output-sensitivity objective. The authors report that it outperforms state-of-the-art transformation and rounding methods in both channel-wise and block-wise settings.

entry.title: Wizard: Real-time, agent-controlled manipulation of any virtual world
entry.summary: Wizard: Manipulate Any World in Real Time via Agentic Control arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents Wizard, an agentic game world model that enables real-time, precise control of character motions and generalizes zero-shot to new scenes, characters, and actions. The authors build a dataset covering 750 scenes and 178 characters, using skeleton and geometry information as structured representations to condition a video generation model. An adaptive masking mechanism improves alignment between these conditioning signals and generated video, while an agentic framework explicitly maintains and updates game states so players can freely configure their virtual worlds.

entry.title: Explaining multistep, multivariate wind power forecasts with GradientSHAP
entry.summary: Multistep and Multivariate Time Series Explainability with GradientSHAP: A Wind Power Case Study arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper adapts the GradientSHAP method to explain multivariate, multistep wind power forecasting models, an area that has been largely unexplored. The authors create new visualizations that give both local and global explanations, showing relationships among environmental factors, site conditions, and temporal patterns. They find that with careful handling of SHAP values and domain expertise, the method yields useful insights into model behaviour. The authors also note that its complexity makes practical deployment difficult.

entry.title: How pretrained language models jointly encode two independently changing temporal variables
entry.summary: Factorized Representations of Concurrent Temporal Variables in Pretrained Language Models arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper studies how language models keep track of several contextual variables that change independently within one document. Using controlled documents with separate language-switch and topic-change timers, the authors find that both timers can be linearly decoded from the same hidden states across ten pretrained checkpoints. The results support an approximate factorization of these representations in overlapping subspaces.

entry.title: Radiology guideline-based decision graph for clinical decision support
entry.summary: Radiology Guideline-derived Decision Graph for Efficient Clinical Decision Support arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces GDGraph, which uses a large language model to split radiology guidelines into sections and build an executable decision graph from extracted subgraphs. At inference, a fast model answers localized clinical questions while deterministic traversal resolves Boolean logic, producing a traceable decision path. On 347 cases covering renal cyst, adnexal mass, and thyroid nodule guidelines, accuracy rose from 57.3% to 90.8%.

entry.title: How to Loop a Transformer: Scaling, Specialization, and Parallel Inference
entry.summary: How to Loop Your Transformer: Loop Scaling, Specialization, and Parallel Inference arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies looping in transformer models, which reuses the same weights by applying a transformer, or part of it, repeatedly to add depth without adding parameters. The authors train dense decoder-only models up to 1B parameters, varying which parts are looped, the number of loops, and how information passes between loops. They find that looping the full model is strongest at a fixed parameter budget, while looping a middle block is better under limited training compute, and that gains from more loops can saturate or become unstable. They also add loop-specific low-rank adapters and modify Parallel Loop Transformers so that quality is preserved while decoding runs in parallel.

entry.title: Accuracy and calibration of Decision and System One AI models on rheumatology exam and diagnosis questions
entry.summary: Decision and System One models in rheumatology: accuracy and calibration on specialty-training examination questions and diagnostic case vignettes arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This study evaluates how accurately several Decision and System One models answer rheumatology examination questions and diagnostic case vignettes, and how well their confidence matches their correctness. On Spanish specialty-training exam questions, most models scored highly, with Jev at 93.0% in Spanish and 91.9% in English, below GPT-6 Sol at 99.4%. On diagnostic vignettes, all System One models scored below GPT-6 Sol at 76.9%, and Jev reached 50.0% while showing overconfidence.

entry.title: Vampire-Hammer: calling an automated prover from the Lean proof assistant
entry.summary: Hammering with Vampire in Lean arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper presents Vampire-Hammer, a tool that lets the Lean interactive theorem prover hand goals to the Vampire automated theorem prover and then checks the resulting proofs with the Lean kernel. It processes goals and premises with the Lean-auto framework and uses standard TPTP and annotated TSTP formats to support proof reconstruction. On 196,083 eligible Mathlib theorems with a 10-second budget, it solves 21,158 problems that the other evaluated tools did not solve within the same time.

entry.title: Textual Response-Aware Guidance for Zero-Shot Adversarial Robustness in Vision-Language Models
entry.summary: Textual Response-Aware Guidance for Zero-Shot Adversarial Robustness of Vision-Language Models arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies how to make vision-language models more resistant to adversarial attacks while keeping their zero-shot performance. It argues that two common guidance methods each have limitations, and proposes TRAG, which constrains visual representation drift using the pre-trained text encoder's responses to local input changes. Experiments across architectures and tasks report state-of-the-art clean and robust performance, and further analysis indicates TRAG helps preserve pre-trained image-text relationships.

entry.title: Rimuru: Unified Memory Management for LLM Serving via Elastic Expert Offloading
entry.summary: Rimuru: Unified Memory Management for Modern LLM Serving via Elastic Expert Offloading arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper addresses device memory pressure in serving large language models, where fixed memory partitions for model weights and attention states cannot adapt to changing workloads. It presents Rimuru, which uses a shared page pool, memory views with per-tensor page sizes, a multi-level page allocator, and a page-table-aware fused MoE kernel to share memory elastically across heterogeneous tensors. A workload-aware adjuster reallocates pages at runtime. Implemented on vLLM, the system is reported to achieve up to 19.03x baseline throughput and a 98.1% average reduction in TTFT.

entry.title: Deep learning with causal constraints for early warning of rapid cyclone intensification in the western North Pacific
entry.summary: Causal-prior-constrained deep learning for rapid-intensification warning of western North Pacific tropical cyclones arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents CausalVisionRI, a deep-learning system that warns of rapid intensification of tropical cyclones over 24 hours in the western North Pacific. It combines infrared satellite imagery, atmospheric and oceanic fields, and a causal graph discovered from observations as a training prior. On a forward holdout test covering 2020 to 2024, its five-member ensemble achieves a Brier skill score of 0.259, outperforming several reference systems. Ablation experiments show that the causal graph pathway improves performance.

entry.title: Self-training with contrast-frame subtraction for coronary X-ray vessel segmentation across hospitals
entry.summary: Self-training for cross-centre coronary vessel segmentation in X-ray angiography using pre-contrast frame subtraction arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper addresses the drop in performance of coronary X-ray angiography vessel segmentation models on data from centres not seen during training. The authors generate pseudo-labels from nnU-Net predictions and a contrast map obtained by subtracting a pre-contrast frame, then self-train without extra manual annotation. Self-training improved results on external datasets, and the size of the gain depended largely on the sensitivity of the model that produced the initial pseudo-labels.

entry.title: MAServeBench: Benchmark for Serving Multi-Agent LLM Systems with Hierarchical Collaboration Workloads
entry.summary: MAServeBench: Benchmarking Multi-Agent LLM Serving Systems with Hierarchical Collaboration Workloads arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents MAServeBench, a benchmark for evaluating serving systems that run multi-agent large language model applications. It treats how agents collaborate and exchange context as a configurable part of the workload, so the same tasks can produce different serving demands. The benchmark records realized operations and dependencies for reproducible comparisons and links them to hardware behavior, showing why higher serving efficiency does not always mean tasks finish sooner.

entry.title: DolphinRouting: Cluster-Level Routing for Split LLM Serving
entry.summary: DolphinRouting: Cluster-Level Binary Routing for Disaggregated LLM Inference Serving arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents DolphinRouting, a method for routing requests in large language model serving systems that separate prefill and decode phases. Requests are grouped into clusters by prompt length, cache-adjusted input lengths, and output-length information, and each cluster learns a binary choice between local and remote prefill from end-to-end SLO feedback. Evaluated on a real disaggregated cluster with public benchmarks, a mixed workload, and real data, the k-means variant reduces P90 TTFT by 5.7 to 7.9% and P90 TPOT by 2.6 to 10.1% compared with Dynamo.

entry.title: Online knapsack with removable items using recourse and size bounds
entry.summary: Leveraging Recourse and Size Bounds for OnlineKnapsack with Removable Items arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies the online unweighted knapsack problem, where items arrive one by one and must be accepted or rejected immediately to maximize the total size of accepted items. It allows previously accepted items to be removed and considers two extensions: knowing an upper bound on item sizes and being able to reinsert previously rejected items. The authors establish close upper and lower bounds on the competitive ratio under these combined assumptions. They also introduce adaptive online algorithms that do not require knowing the size upper bound yet achieve comparable performance guarantees.

entry.title: Only Accepted Tokens Count: Energy Accounting of Speculative Decoding Under Latency Targets
entry.summary: Only Accepted Tokens Count: An Energy Accounting of Speculative Decoding Under Latency Targets arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper examines the energy cost of speculative decoding, in which a drafter proposes several future tokens that a target model verifies in one forward pass. The energy saving depends on how many drafted tokens are accepted, which varies by model, drafting scheme, and text. Measured on H100 and H200 GPUs with SGLang at batch sizes up to 64 across 5 corpora, the saving shrinks as batch size grows and can become a loss at large batches. Speculation only adds energy savings when acceptance is high.

entry.title: LoRe-MIM: A self-supervised method for learning features from whole-body PET/CT scans using masked image reconstruction
entry.summary: LoRe-MIM: Lost-or-Replaced Masked Image Modeling for Self-Supervised Representation Learning in Whole-Body PET/CT arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper addresses the shortage of expert annotations for whole-body PET/CT deep learning by assembling a multi-tracer, multi-institutional dataset of 6,531 scans. It proposes LoRe-MIM, a self-supervised framework that learns multimodal representations by reconstructing masked images, where masked regions are either zeroed out (Lost) or replaced with the corresponding complementary imaging modality (Replaced). The learned representations are evaluated on tasks including multimodal reconstruction, cancer versus non-cancer patch classification, whole-body lesion segmentation, label-efficient training, and robustness assessment. The authors report that LoRe-MIM consistently outperforms corresponding state-of-the-art baselines across these tasks.

entry.title: Guiding latent reasoning exploration with potential-based trajectory balance
entry.summary: Latent Path Exploration via Potential-Guided Subtrajectory Balance arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces SubLAT, a method for continuous latent reasoning in language models that combines a relative answer potential with Subtrajectory Balance to learn stochastic latent exploration. The model is trained jointly with answer supervision, CoT supervision, and representation distillation. Experiments on arithmetic and deductive reasoning show that solution coverage increases with larger sampling budgets and improves on several structural out-of-distribution benchmarks.

entry.title: Self-supervised brain encoders that align across people in fMRI
entry.summary: Latent Prediction Yields Cross-Subject Alignable Representations in Sensory-Evoked fMRI arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper adapts a joint embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) to learn participant-specific fMRI encoders from brain data alone, without ever seeing stimulus images. On the Natural Scenes Dataset (NSD), the embeddings achieve competitive results on brain captioning and image reconstruction against supervised pipelines that use images and language. The authors also show that encoders for different participants can be aligned fully unsupervised, so a decoding head trained on one participant transfers to another without fine-tuning while keeping most of its within-subject performance.

entry.title: Neighborhood Elites: Quality-Diversity Search for Detecting Wrong Answers in QA
entry.summary: Neighborhood Elites: Quality-Diversity Search for Uncertainty Quantification in Question Answering arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper addresses the difficulty of detecting wrong answers from large language models in question answering. It proposes neighborhood elites (NE), a method that uses quality-diversity search to build answer-preserving input rewrites spread across two axes: the kind of edit and how explicitly the context supports the answer. Across five extractive-QA datasets and five instruction-tuned LLMs, NE improves failure detection over other neighborhood constructors in at least 24 of 25 pairs, and also outperforms semantic entropy computed over decoder samples.

entry.title: TaskFrame: A Framework Linking Task Planning to Frame-Level Control for Game Agents
entry.summary: TaskFrame: Connecting Task-Level Planning with Frame-Level Control for Game Agents arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents TaskFrame, a hierarchical framework for game agents that connects task-level planning with frame-level keyboard and mouse control. A vision-language planner breaks a high-level goal into ordered atomic instructions, while a causal Transformer controller predicts actions at each game step using the active goal and recent observations. Experiments in Minecraft show competitive instruction decomposition compared with general-purpose vision-language models, and a higher combat success rate than the evaluated baselines in closed-loop evaluation.

entry.title: From MS/MS Evidence to Adaptive Spectroscopy: Reinforcement Learning Guided by Candidate Structures
entry.summary: From MS/MS evidence to adaptive spectroscopic characterization: Reinforcement learning guided by candidate molecular structures arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper proposes a structure-informed deep Q-network (SI-DQN) that uses existing MS/MS evidence to decide whether further characterization is needed, which measurement to request, and when to stop. The policy was evaluated on a Multimodal Spectroscopic Dataset containing simulated MS/MS, infrared, and NMR spectra. Results show higher Top-1 accuracy with far fewer additional measurements than complete acquisition, and lower composite loss than a rule-based policy.

entry.title: Learned terminal costs enable short-horizon MPC for autonomous trucks in busy highway traffic
entry.summary: Learned Terminal Costs for Short-Horizon Model Predictive Control of Autonomous Trucks in Interactive Highway Traffic arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper addresses autonomous highway driving for heavy-duty trucks, combining Model Predictive Control (MPC) with Reinforcement Learning (RL). A finite-horizon MPC solved by dynamic programming uses a pre-trained RL model to estimate terminal cost. The method is tested in simulation with reactive surrounding traffic against pure MPC with zero terminal cost, rollout with a base-policy terminal cost, and pure RL. The hybrid approach achieves zero collisions and the lowest cost among all configurations.

entry.title: When Requirements Interact: Long-Horizon Coding via Interdependent Specs
entry.summary: When Requirements Interact: Scaling Long-Horizon Coding via Interdependent Specifications arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces CodeSpecWeave, a framework that synthesizes coding tasks with rich, interdependent specifications grounded in real developer seeds. A synthesis agent creates coupled requirements and executable tests, while a review agent audits solution trajectories from multiple models to ensure test reliability. The authors built 4,670 training tasks across 2,865 repositories and used reinforcement learning on them, substantially outperforming the base model and existing baselines on DeepSWE-v1.1. They also released CodeSpecWeave-Bench, a benchmark of 100 tasks and 1,044 specifications.

entry.title: Statistical Analysis of Verified Synthetic Data in Linear Regression
entry.summary: Statistical Analysis of Synthetic Data with Verification: A Linear Regression Framework arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies self-training on synthetic data within a linear regression framework. A pre-trained estimator generates data with injected noise, a verifier filters samples by a threshold, and the model is then fine-tuned on accepted samples. The authors derive finite-sample risk bounds across four regimes to show how verification threshold, generation noise, and pre-training error affect prediction risk.

entry.title: Estimating ground speed from Doppler spectra with per-frame confidence
entry.summary: Confidence-Aware Speed-over-Ground Estimation from Doppler Spectra via Reconstruction-Based Representation Learning arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper proposes a method for estimating speed over ground from ground-facing Doppler spectra, aimed at mobile platforms such as railway systems. It builds on an autoencoder reconstruction approach, adding a speed estimation head on the latent features and a lightweight confidence head used at inference, with noise augmentation training. Experiments show improved speed estimation accuracy over classical baselines and confidence estimates that indicate the reliability of individual predictions under adverse signal conditions.

entry.title: Conformal annotation with randomized expert review for online cell-type labeling
entry.summary: Conformal Annotation with Randomized Expert Review: Application to Online Cell-Type Labeling arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper proposes CARED, a distribution-free framework for AI-assisted cell-type annotation under distribution shift. It randomly selects cases for expert review and uses the resulting labels to calibrate later decisions. The authors prove long-run control of cumulative error without stationarity or exchangeability assumptions. Experiments on pancreas, lung, and ovary annotation streams show that up to 70% of cells can bypass expert review while errors remain controlled.

entry.title: Distribution-calibrated, budget-neutral token credit for multimodal RL with verifiable rewards
entry.summary: Distributional Reward Calibration and Budget-Neutral Credit Assignment for Multimodal RLVR arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper proposes TACE, a two-stage estimator for advantage computation in GRPO. The first stage maps rewards to a standard normal via a one-dimensional optimal-transport map to align reward distributions across tasks and cap outliers. The second stage rank-calibrates token-level evidence weights within each trajectory and renormalizes them to mean one, conserving total credit and sign. On a multimodal reasoning suite, TACE achieves the best results on most benchmarks but not in every setting.

entry.title: Reaction precedents let retrosynthesis prediction go beyond its training data
entry.summary: Reaction precedents extend retrosynthetic prediction beyond training coverage arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper examines how far retrieved reaction precedents can make up for gaps in a retrosynthesis model's task-specific training coverage. Using 2.71 million reactions, the authors limited training and retrieval by transformation type or time, then expanded only the retrieval corpus while keeping model parameters fixed. Precedents substantially raised accuracy on transformations excluded from training and improved all 14 general-purpose models, with the best surpassing eight specialized models.

entry.title: LLM-guided planar loco-manipulation for quadruped robots using language planning and pushing policies
entry.summary: LLM-guided Planar Loco-Manipulation for Quadruped Robots arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper addresses robotic navigation in cluttered environments where reaching a goal may require physically moving obstacles. A language-conditioned task planner, fine-tuned with LoRA on synthetic data, generates variable-length sequences of parameterized actions executed by low-level reinforcement-learning policies. The planner outperforms a classical planner and a prompted frontier model on interactive navigation tasks. An end-to-end whole-body planar pushing policy reaches a 93.3% success rate in simulation, compared with 83.5% for a hierarchical baseline.

entry.title: EnvOS: Auditing AI computer agents in software that changes mid-task
entry.summary: EnvOS: Auditing Computer-Use Agents When the World Moves On : Phenomenon-Based Task Construction, Certification, and Evidence-Based Evaluation arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces EnvOS, a framework for building and certifying environments whose software changes while an AI agent is working on a task. It checks before a run that changes fire correctly and tasks remain solvable, and re-checks verdicts from archived evidence afterward. Tested on stale-information scenarios in clinic booking and insurance-claim approval, the results show that whether an agent notices a change depends on the model and the interface shown to it.

entry.title: ScienceJudge: Pattern-Based Data Augmentation for Checking Sentence-Level Scientific Claims
entry.summary: ScienceJudge: Pattern Perturbation Augmentation for Sentence-Level Scientific Claim Verification arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper addresses checking whether each sentence in an AI-generated scientific paragraph is supported by a given multimodal evidence bundle. The authors propose Pattern Perturbation Augmentation (PPA), which models reporting errors as faithfulness-breaking transformations to create hard negative examples. Their ScienceJudge system combines vision-language and LLM predictors, raising the local development-set average score from 0.8124 to 0.8692. It ranked first on the official NLPCC 2026 Task 10 Track 1 leaderboard with a final score of 0.6890.

entry.title: Mining translation pairs from linguistic archives for low-resource languages
entry.summary: Mobilizing the Archive: Bitext Extraction at Scale from Archival Documents for Extremely Low-resource Languages arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper proposes extracting parallel translation examples from linguistic archival materials such as grammars and dictionaries, which cover languages with little online presence. The authors build a pipeline combining an OCR model and a vision language model so that extracted text stays aligned with visual layout information. The extracted bitexts are used across 20 languages to train machine translation models and to support in-context learning for large language models. For in-context learning, the reported chrF2++ gains over zero-shot translation are +15.78 for low-resource and +6.94 for high-resource target languages.

entry.title: EpiAgent: Epistemic Self-Play Framework for LLM Agents
entry.summary: EpiAgent: Epistemic Self-Play for LLM Agents arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper proposes EpiAgent, a framework that gives LLM-based agents a learnable layer for maintaining beliefs about others' private information. The policy is split into an Epistemic Update stage and an Action Planning stage, optimized alternately through a bi-level formulation called Epistemic Self-Play, using an intrinsic prediction reward. The authors report that EpiAgent outperforms prompting-based and RL-based baselines in mixed and competitive scenarios.

entry.title: Benchmark testing whether multimodal LLMs judge color accurately against CIE-computed ground truth
entry.summary: Benchmarking color judgment in multimodal LLMs with CIE-computable ground truth arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper introduces a five-task benchmark built on the CIE colorimetric framework, covering white-balance pair judgment, skin-tone bias direction, correlated color temperature estimation, CIE Delta E 2000 pair ordering, and color naming under changing illuminants. Eight multimodal LLM endpoints were tested. The models often handle coarse binary white-balance judgments but perform weakly on numeric color temperature estimation and some fine color-difference tasks.

entry.title: Error attribution and depth-aware safety evaluation for monocular RGB human tracking in robot navigation
entry.summary: Decision-Level Error Attribution and Depth-Aware Safety Evaluation of Monocular RGB Human Tracking for Autonomous Robot Navigation arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies monocular RGB human tracking used for robot stop-or-proceed safety decisions. The authors prove that a lateral-only distance rule cannot miss dangers flagged by a planar distance rule, but it causes unnecessary stops. Using ETH and UCY pedestrian videos with simulated stationary robots, they apply a two-factor Shapley attribution to separate rule and perception error contributions.

entry.title: Entity-anchored claim extraction for mining arguments in full-text research papers
entry.summary: Towards Full-Text Scholarly Argument Mining using Entity-Anchored Claim Extraction arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper proposes using scientific entity mentions such as tasks, datasets, and models to identify and structure claims in full-text scholarly articles. A case study on 50 sentiment analysis papers yields a human gold standard and a silver-standard dataset of 1,487 claims, generated by majority voting among large language models. Encoders fine-tuned only on the silver-standard data outperform those trained on the small human-annotated set and transfer zero-shot to NLP papers outside the training corpus.

entry.title: Combining graph structure and text meaning to predict links in text-attributed graphs
entry.summary: Bridging Semantics and Structure: A Theoretically Grounded Framework for Link Prediction on TAGs arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper proposes Bridge-LP, a framework for link prediction on text-attributed graphs that unifies graph and language representations. It combines three components: a jumping connection of textual proximity, compressed embeddings that encode neighborhood information, and a cache embedding training strategy that reduces computation. The authors compare against 40 existing models on 9 datasets and report up to a 43.06% improvement in Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR).

entry.title: Combining video generation with agent harnesses: agentic video creation, agentic world modeling, and recursive self-improvement
entry.summary: Video Generation Meets Agent Harness: Agentic Video Generation, Agentic World Modeling and Recursive Self-Improvement arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This report is a review of how video generation can be combined with agent harnesses, which are executable runtimes that manage context, tools, state, feedback, and budgets. It examines three directions: agentic video generation, where harnesses coordinate scripting, shot planning, production, and editing; agentic world modeling, where harnesses mediate observation, control, and state; and recursive self-improvement in video model development. It also analyzes the agent capabilities involved and discusses open challenges such as autonomous production, lifelong memory, and evaluation.

entry.title: AdMuse: Skill-Guided Creative Advertising Image Generation
entry.summary: AdMuse: Skill-Guided Creative Advertising Image Generation arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper presents AdMuse, a multi-agent framework that distills high-quality advertisements into reusable creative skills for cross-domain advertising strategy. At generation time, it routes suitable skills, produces and selects among multiple candidate concepts, and refines the final image with vision-language feedback. Experiments across diverse product and brand positionings show that AdMuse produces visually compelling ads that communicate product positioning.

entry.title: Analyzing axial attention in time series foundation models using single location regression
entry.summary: Understanding axial attention in TSFMs through single location regression arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper extends the Single Location Regression framework to two-dimensional structured data to study sparse settings where a target depends on a few tokens. The authors formulate an analytically tractable axial attention-type predictor and analyze its statistical properties and training dynamics. They prove that, under a specific asymptotic regime and with known oracle parameters, the predictor is Bayes optimal, while certain semi-linear simplifications are not. For a specific temperature scaling, projected gradient descent is shown to converge globally to the optimal parameters, and experiments confirm the importance of inverse temperature scheduling.

entry.title: Finding and Filling Information Gaps in Multi-Agent Systems
entry.summary: Locating and Closing Information Gaps in Multi-Agent Systems arXiv · Oct 29, 2026Multi-step web tasks often need several LLM agents to gather and combine evidence, but a fixed workflow's communication links may prevent needed evidence from reaching the agent that uses it, producing incomplete or wrong answers. The paper proposes SPLICE, which locates a possible gap for each query, adds one directed edge to deliver the relevant evidence, and re-runs the affected nodes to produce a candidate answer. A selector trained on process features then decides whether to adopt the candidate or keep the original answer. On five benchmarks, SPLICE improves web tool-use task score by 8.0% and the mean score on four reasoning and planning benchmarks by 5.7% over the static skeleton, at 1.25 to 1.44 times its cost, and transfers zero-shot to four unseen backbones.

entry.title: Hidden Ranking Disparities: Category-Aware Fairness via Distributional Stability
entry.summary: Hidden Disparities in Ranking: Category-Aware Fairness via Distributional Stability arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies fair ranking in recommender systems by modeling ranking policies as distributions over permutations, with user utility measured as the exposure of interacted items relative to an ideal ranking. It introduces utility parity across user groups and a category-aware variant, conditional utility parity, and shows both are equivalent to stability of utility under changes in group composition. Optimizing over mixtures of ranking policies yields a second-order cone program, for which generalization bounds are provided. A numerical study validates the theoretical findings.

entry.title: Beyond CCT: Per-shot camera color correction by recovering illuminant spectra
entry.summary: Beyond CCT: Multi-channel SPD recovery for per-shot camera color correction arXiv · Oct 29, 2026Cameras usually correct color with pre-calibrated matrices interpolated by correlated color temperature (CCT), which reduces the light source to a single number. This paper instead recovers the illuminant's spectral power distribution using non-negative least squares, a basis dictionary, the camera white point, and a multi-channel ambient light sensor, then fits a 3x3 color correction matrix for each shot. On a synthetic benchmark of 300 illuminants and 3,100 reflectances, mean angular error falls from 1.89 to 1.20 degrees, with about a 1.7x tail reduction for LED-like off-Planckian illuminants.

entry.title: EventSeeColor: Reconstructing Color Images from Monochrome Event Data
entry.summary: EventSeeColor: Learning to Reconstruct Color from Monochrome Events arXiv · Oct 29, 2026Event cameras record brightness changes under difficult lighting, but traditional event-based reconstruction yields only grayscale images. This paper presents EventSeeColor, which uses reconstructed grayscale images and aligned events to jointly guide a diffusion colorizer. In a combined evaluation on two real event datasets, it achieves the best structural similarity, learned perceptual scores, and chromatic-region color difference among the compared external methods.

entry.title: Fisher Contrastive Learning to reduce feature suppression, tested on leukemia diagnosis
entry.summary: Fisher Contrastive Learning to Mitigate Feature Suppression: A Case Study in Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia Diagnosis arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper introduces Fisher Contrastive Learning (FCL), which uses a regularized Fisher trace criterion to counter feature suppression in self-supervised contrastive learning, where dominant features overshadow other class-relevant signals. The authors prove that FCL's learned representations alleviate this effect. FCL is tested on simulated benchmarks and on pretraining with white blood cell microscopy images, then transferred to diagnosing acute promyelocytic leukemia in an external cohort. It outperforms self-supervised baselines, yielding more robust and discriminative representations.

entry.title: A Negotiation-Aware Hybrid LLM Framework for Intent Interpretation and Service Discovery
entry.summary: A Negotiation-Aware Hybrid LLM Framework for Intent Interpretation and Service Discovery arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper proposes a framework that interprets natural-language cloud intents, which may be incomplete or conflicting, and discovers matching services. The framework refines the intent and detects conflicts, structures it into a provider-independent TOSCA template, and retrieves candidate offers by deterministic matching against cloud provider catalogs. Conflicts are resolved through iterative natural-language negotiation with the user. On 70 diverse intents, it improved conflict detection and service discovery recall and F1 over single-shot and enhanced-prompting baselines, and eliminated hallucinated offers.

entry.title: FARE: Factor-Aware Retrieval with Error-Guided Fusion for Retail Forecasting
entry.summary: FARE: Factor-Aware Retrieval with Error-Guided Fusion for Retail Forecasting arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper introduces FARE, a method for forecasting retail sales, where promotions and calendar events shift short-term demand. It retrieves historical weeks separately for each known factor of the target week and merges them into a factor reference, then uses two gates to blend this with a shape reference and correct a backbone forecast. Across the Favorita, M5, Rossmann, and Rohlik datasets, FARE reduces the weighted absolute percentage error of five backbone models by 11.46%, 4.06%, 14.63%, and 10.16% on average.

entry.title: Training-free online method that breaks video into steps for step grounding
entry.summary: Hierarchical Step Decomposition for Training-free Online Video Step Grounding arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper proposes Hierarchical Step Decomposition (HSD), a training-free framework for online Video Step Grounding that uses Large Multimodal Models. HSD groups streaming video segments into semantically coherent events and refines uncertain step predictions by decomposing candidate steps into finer substeps. The authors report that HSD outperforms state-of-the-art methods on HT-Step, Ego4D Goal-Step, and CrossTask, with better recognition, more accurate localization, and faster inference.

entry.title: The Generative Paradox: An Anti-Prompt Approach to Human Capability
entry.summary: The generative paradox: the Anti-Prompt paradigm for human capability arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper argues that generative AI in education is usually judged only by human-AI team output, overlooking whether people can still understand, challenge, and repair work when assistance changes or disappears. It introduces the "generative paradox" and proposes treating retained human capability as a design goal alongside joint performance. The Anti-Prompt paradigm reverses the usual interaction order, so AI first creates conditions for human construction when immediate generation would preempt a consequential human act.

entry.title: Mode Dynamics: A framework linking neural network parameter changes to output behavior
entry.summary: Mode Dynamics: A Framework for Neural Network Learning arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper introduces Mode Dynamics, a framework that links coordinated parameter motion during neural network training to changes in model outputs. It decomposes recorded parameter updates into collective modes and measures each mode's effect on outputs. Experiments show that a few leading modes can reconstruct behavior, induced effects depend on the training path, and modal complexity varies with task and data.

entry.title: A deep learning method for predicting demand ranges in online retail when sales data is capped and boosted
entry.summary: A Deep Learning Framework for Quantile Demand Forecasting in E-commerce with Doubly Censored Data arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper presents a deep learning framework that learns quantiles from doubly censored observations, where sales are limited by stock and raised by promotions while the target is underlying demand. It also proposes a tailored evaluation metric that correlates well with the oracle calibration measure. The authors provide theoretical guarantees and report that their estimator outperforms existing baselines. Inventory simulations and real-world applications confirm its practical value in retail operations.

entry.title: NeurEO: Using Neuroscience Methods to Interpret Earth Observation Embeddings
entry.summary: NeurEO: dissecting Earth observation embeddings with computational neuroscience arXiv · Oct 29, 2026Earth embeddings compress rich Earth observation data so downstream models can handle many geospatial tasks, but their meaning is unclear. The authors adapt computational neuroscience methods, usually used to interpret neural activity, to analyse AlphaEarth embeddings. They examine embedding features alone and against land cover and elevation, finding correlational and multi-scale structure and specific directional tuning such as a "North vs South woodland edge" response. Removing the main land cover trends reveals finer-grained representational details with higher effective dimensionality.

entry.title: DynaRev: A Benchmark for Testing Web Agents When User Goals Change Mid-Task
entry.summary: DynaRev: Benchmarking Web Agents under Dynamic Goal Revision arXiv · Oct 29, 2026DynaRev is a benchmark of 181 tasks for evaluating web agents whose goals are revised during execution, rather than fixed in advance. Revisions are delivered at task-defined semantic milestones and include additive revisions, unconditional overrides, and runtime-conditioned overrides. Evaluation covers correctness, responsiveness, and efficiency using trajectory-based analysis, and tests of five models show agents often satisfy only part of the task requirements.

entry.title: VideoMemBench: How Well Multimodal Models Remember Across Video Dialogue Turns
entry.summary: VideoMemBench: How Well Do MLLMs Remember in Video Conversations? arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper introduces VideoMemBench, a benchmark testing whether multimodal large language models can retain and reuse information from earlier turns in a multi-turn conversation about one video. It contains 326 videos and 2,476 turns, 1,387 of which depend on earlier turns. Among over 20 evaluated models, the best, Claude Opus 5, scores only 45.7% overall.
